## The state of the novel, in one paragraph

**Four hundred chapters in eight closed volumes, and the manuscript is 1,091,877 words, of which 1,079,283 is everything through Chapter 390 and 12,594 is Volume 08's fifth and last movement. The seven closed volumes reproduce to the word at 202,117 / 184,039 / 176,097 / 148,821 / 144,248 / 101,261 / 72,149, and Volume 08 stands at 63,145 across fifty chapters in five movements of 15,506 / 11,208 / 11,365 / 12,472 / 12,594.** A male legal clerk, Marek Kest, thirty-eight, audits inheritance and guild contracts in an empire where dragon Houses have spent four volumes turning private promises into public obligations. **Seven volumes in, the machinery stopped. Volume 08 was the cost of that, fifty weeks, one ordinary week to a chapter, and nothing in it changed. Fifty weeks is what the volume has now shown: the price is a number of people, the arrangement is still standing, and one of the people paying it is the man the series is about.** The last of those weeks is a woman of twenty-four at a counter at the top of four flights who has been ready for two years and is not told what she is standing ready for, and the last line of the volume is that nothing is asked of anybody. **`outline/volume-09.md` exists and is the outline of record for Chapters 0401 to 0450 and is titled *The Blank*, and this file's own claim that it did not exist stood here until the repair named above and is not deleted. The plan that outline is built against is `outline/series.md`, and the series plan's Volume 09 block — a coalition, a constitutional convention, a provisional charter, an offer of leadership, a named antagonist's emergency clause, a hall, a mountain and a climax — is declared against by name, field by field, in the declarations section near the foot of that outline, and no chapter of Volume 09 may inherit any of it.**

## Who is alive, who wants what, and what each of them is refused

**Marek Kest, thirty-eight, the protagonist.** He holds nothing: no office, no fund, no list, no leave, no stage, and no certification at any point in eight volumes. He refuses the reading, does not exercise the thing he is able to do, and his reason for not reaching a stage is in about nine words on a page and is not paid a second time. He wants the erased name of his mother and the disputed family claim, and he has neither, and **the name of the hand that struck the line out of the leaf in his coat is in his head and on no paper and is printed in no chapter of Volume 08, and the who is Volume 06's and goes on unanswered, and unanswered is not the same as closed.** **He is on the page in eleven of Volume 08's fifty chapters, which is 1 / 1 / 3 / 3 / 3 across the five movements against a floor of three, so the floor is met in the last three movements and missed in the first two, and in person he stands in six of the fifty — 0355, 0365, 0371, 0379, 0390 and 0399, one in each of four movements and two in Movement Three. Both figures were re-derived by this phase from the fifty files and both reproduce; the count the close printed as four was an uncounted figure and is named and not deleted.** Nobody asked him one thing, nobody thanked him, and the woman about four miles off at the top of a stair is still not told anything.

**The protagonist's mother, dead on the roll and not dead on the page, gone twelve years in the Ashfall Archive fire.** **Her name is printed in this record, and in every document this phase wrote, nowhere: it stands only in superseded headers in `state/archive/current-md-superseded.md` and in the closed volumes' own earlier records.** **Her name is printed in none of Volume 08's fifty chapters, and the name that ought to stand at the end of the struck line is printed in none of them either, and the name of the hand that struck it is not printed anywhere in this project outside one man's head.** Her name comes back in Volume 12 and she is not turned into an infallible martyr when it does.

**Bren Kest, alive, Marek's father, a locksmith in Greyfen.** He does not understand dragon law and refuses to pretend that he does. He is in none of Volume 08's fifty files and nothing in them moved him.

**Nell Kest, twenty, Marek's sister, a dye-house worker about four hundred and thirty miles up this river.** Sixteen volumes in a counting room, fifteen on loan, the one with her own name in capitals at the head of it, unopened. **A wage of nineteen days of a crew's money is still held in a coat four miles off, in a room she has not stood in since she was seventeen, and a notice with a printed ruled space on the back of it is in the same pocket with the space clean.** The coat went four miles and came back four miles and the money is the same. A rule said once in a lane lives in her and not in the woman who said it. Nobody paid her, nobody sent for her, nobody thanked her, nobody forgave her, the rule was not given to a third woman, **and she is not going to ask what it is held against, and she is not going up this river this season and a season is not a life.**

**Tamsin Rook, twenty-four, at the fourth counter, two years, not a lawyer.** **Nobody has ever put a question to her in two years, and in Chapter 0400, the last chapter of the volume, a colleague told her out loud that a person who has been ready for two years has made herself the only thing in that room that can be said something to, and that readiness is not a form and cannot be entered on anything, and that the day somebody at the top of those four flights finds out is the day she gets used.** She did not exercise the undertaking of the fourth of the first month, did not retire it, **did not say the date out loud, and it has not been said out loud in two years and is not said out loud by a state record either.** She did one smaller thing, at a quarter past the fourth hour: **she took her apron off the hook and hung it up again, because she had come in twenty minutes early for two years and there had been no need to.** The drawer under the board is shut, there are four things in it and two she has never opened, the box of about four hundred blanks stands three inches further forward than it stood ten weeks ago, and the last line of the volume is that nothing is asked of anybody.

**Marn Ottery, thirty-four, at the other end of the same counter, eleven years, not a lawyer.** About four hundred bought and unfilled blanks under the far end of those boards, unopened in six years, and no form ever drawn to account for them. **In 0391 she moved that box four inches and then an inch back, and a young man from the shipping floor told her out loud that a clerk who moves a box is a clerk who has made a statement about it, and she said the statement was hers and that nobody had asked her for a decision. In 0400 she told Tamsin Rook the plainest thing anybody says to her in four chapters, and entered that she was saying it as a woman telling a colleague and not as somebody with any standing to do one thing about it.** She is the only other person in that building who knows what is in that drawer, and the arrangement that makes that true is what she wants, and it is not on the page as a want and is not to be printed as one. She is not thanked, and in 0400 she says in terms that she is not going to be thanked for it.

**Halla Wray, fifty-one, a foreman at the Slade end, entered there by a class, which is a heading.** **A form that would take the two of seventeen at the back of that shed out of the back of it has been on the board since the tenth month and will be on it again on the second of the two days next week, and no one in that lane has the standing to find anything void, because nothing in this empire has ever been asked to be void and there is no procedure for asking.** In 0395 she got as far as saying out loud that it had been there a month, and the man of about twenty-eight stopped her a third time and gave a third reason and it was the plainest of the three. She said nothing. **The two of seventeen are still on that bench, the girl was not given the chance to say no, the man of about fifty-five with the chain said his four sentences and nobody answered him and he never wanted an answer, the lamp was not lit until the seventh hour, and the second half of a sentence she began in a doorway has still not arrived.**

**Rennick Adley, thirty-eight, the Company's book-keeper, four hundred yards up the lane off the Slade.** Wants the rest of a sentence and has not asked and is not going to. **In 0398 he wrote the same four lines out for the eleventh time and they came out the same and he stopped where they stop, and the clerk of about twenty-nine did not say a second thing, having said once that she would not.** She told him out loud that the woman at the Slade end is still in a box that a class put her in, that a box entered by a class does not come out of itself, that there is nobody he could tell and no form for telling and no standing for telling, and that the not telling is not a decision he made this week. She also said the one thing in those ten chapters about Marek Kest: that he is the only person anybody knows of who could walk down that lane without it being a record of it, and that he is not in that building. He did not walk the four hundred yards and nobody thanked anybody.

**The man of about thirty-four with the fair hand.** Copies other men's figures until two sets agree, four days a season, on somebody's list. **He is the only person in this matter anybody could put a question to and the one nobody has, and the next asking is his and it is nobody's yet.** A number lives in his head that he has never written down and never passed on, and a form with a printed heading over a ruled space came through his letter slot in 0389 and was not returned. **In 0397 he told the woman next door that there is no form for the second knock of the two, that she has made herself responsible for the not knocking, and that he has put it on her because he has nobody he could hand it to and nothing he could fill in.** He filled in nothing, told her nothing about where he has been, and the number is not printed, not confirmed and not denied.

**The man of about sixty-one, the second hand since he was forty-two.** Signs at the foot of about nine hundred sheets a year and cannot read a paragraph. **About nine of them a year are not what the person above him wrote, he signed every one, and he is the only person alive who knows which and cannot write one down.** In 0396 a young man of about twenty-six who is paid by the corner and not for a page told him out loud that a second true thing is in him, that it will come out in about four months, and that the corridor with the hook in the wall is the only place it will happen. **He answered once, to the pen pot: a man does not get the pen out twice in a week for a thing he did not do the first time.** The second true thing did not arrive, his own figure is neither confirmed nor denied, no coming was dated or counted by anybody who can be held to it, and the nine miles is not walked.

**The clerk of about fifty-three, nineteen years in one room off the old river road.** Writes the minutes, advises nobody, asks nothing. Her own finding is on a shelf under a window with no pane in it: a question with no full stop and her own name at the foot, the only thing on that shelf with a name at the foot. **She is the only person in this matter anybody could serve a question on in writing, she made herself askable on purpose in 0390, and in 0392 she said one true thing out loud in that room that is not about the sheets — it was about the weather — and the woman of about nineteen wrote none of it down and has said nothing about it since.** The woman of about nineteen told her out loud that a person who tells is a person who has to go on telling, and that the not being asked has now cost her the only thing she had, which was not being asked, and she did not answer it. **She did not walk the four hundred yards of her own passage in 0392, and a man of thirty-eight who came the whole of that distance once in 0390 has not been in that building since.** Her own question stays a question with no full stop and nobody has asked her a second time.

**The woman of about twenty-six at the lock end of about four hundred yards of cold flags.** Four years at that lock, never one of the three clerks, never sent for, thanked or handed a sheet. Keeps a figure in her head that is on no paper, is not printed in any form, is not handed to anybody, has gone up, and **does not get a heading.** In 0393 nothing with a heading on it came down that passage in a week, and the man in the felt apron told her out loud that the arrangement is the arrangement and that she is the only person at that end who could turn one coming into something that costs her. She said out loud, once, to the passage, that she is not going to be a person who waits for the next one. The count has not gone down and the four hundred yards is not walked. **Two claims in this row were false against the page and are corrected here, and the wrong ones are named and deleted nowhere. It said she was at the end of that passage, and it said the room at the far end of it was not entered. She is at the lock, and the room with the rail is at the other end of the same four hundred yards and is not hers. Chapter 0358's title says so — *A Passage Four Hundred Yards Long Off A Flood Terrace At The Back Of A Building Off The Old River Road, Racks Going Down It And Coming Back Light By One, A Lock At One End And A Room With A Rail At The Other, And A Woman Of Twenty-Six Who Counts In Her Head* — and 0393 says it in a line and not in a title: she knows the sound of that rack arriving at this end of the passage and has been standing at the lock when it comes, and the rail at the other end has nothing on it and has not had anything on it since before she came. The room at the far end is entered, twice a week, by the woman of about forty with a scuttle, and it is where Chapter 0362 happens.** The false placement was not only false. It put this woman in the other woman's room, which is a merge this project has spent a volume preventing.

**The woman who keeps the ground floor of a rented house, about twenty years at the bottom of those stairs, never once above the second one, who takes a rent and has never had his name and has never given him hers.** **She is the second person in this matter known to be keeping a thing with no form on it, and she is not the clerk of about fifty-three: the clerk keeps minutes about four hundred yards off the old river road and has been in that room nineteen years, and this one has never been inside that building and does not know what was said in it.** Chapter 0399's first draft had the two in one mouth; the page is repaired and the separation is in the paragraph that introduces her.

**The woman of about thirty-five next door, the woman of about forty with a scuttle, the woman of about thirty-five with a day-book, the woman of about twenty-two in her second season, the woman of about nineteen who keeps minutes under the clerk, the clerk of about twenty-nine at the other end of two joined tables, and the man in the felt apron.** Each is a person and not a device. **The claim that stood here, that the woman of about forty with a scuttle is in none of Volume 08's fifty files, was false against the page and is named here and deleted nowhere. She is in fourteen of the four hundred closed chapter files: three in Volume 06 (0296, 0297, 0300), ten in Volume 07 (0301, 0307, 0312, 0320, 0321, 0323, 0324, 0336, 0340, 0346), and Chapter 0362 in Volume 08, which is titled *The End Of Four Hundred Yards Of Cold Flags, A Lamp, And A Woman Of Forty Nobody Can Ask* and is set in the room with the rail from its first paragraph to its last.** What the page gives her and nothing more: she is about forty, she is not one of the three clerks and never has been, she goes up that passage twice a week with a scuttle and a lamp and a cloth and lights the lamp, and that is the whole of what she does in it; the other day of that week she is at a washhouse two streets off where there is no rail and nobody says a thing out loud in front of her, and she has said herself that the two halves of her week are not the same trade and are not the same woman and has never tried to make them into one thing; in 0362 she says a true thing out loud to the clerk of about thirty who keeps the rota, he decides not to write it down and says that he made that decision, and nobody thanks her for a lamp and four hundred yards and nothing in this empire sets down that anybody must be. **She is not the woman of about twenty-six, the twenty-six-year-old stands at the lock, and the two are never in one room.** The instruction that survives the correction is the part that was always the point: **a Volume 09 writer may not give her a room, a trade, a week or a history the page has not given her, may not discover her where she was not, and Chapter 0362 is where she was and is the only Volume 08 chapter she is in.** The day-book has a printed heading over every column, no fifth column ruled in nine years, and was not read.

## What runs

**`workspace/volume-09/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`, and it is the only next phase, and it is the first chapter batch of Volume 09, Chapters 0401 to 0410, and it is Movement One of five.** The phase before it was `workspace/volume-09/volume-09-outline/`, and that phase planned the volume: it wrote `outline/volume-09.md`, 111,429 bytes across 265 lines, titled *The Blank*, the first outline of record this project has for a volume since Volume 07, and it created no chapter and wrote no batch card. **`outline/volume-09.md` does exist, and this file's own claim that no phase has written it stood here until the repair named above and is not deleted.** The series plan's Volume 09 block — a coalition, a constitutional convention, a provisional charter, an offer of leadership, a named antagonist's emergency clause, a hall, a mountain and a climax — **is a series-level plan that this page has never used, and the Volume 07 and Volume 08 outlines each declared the same block false in eleven ways in their own heads, and the Volume 09 outline declares all eleven of them again by name, which are the block's own title and its ten fields, which is the pattern it followed and not a new one.**

**And the selection condition, re-measured, because the one this section used to carry had already resolved and the record did not say so.** The walk at `scripts/novel_runner.sh` lines 26 to 40 takes every `PROMPT.md` under `workspace` in sorted path order, skips a directory holding `.retired` or whose prompt opens with a retired-phase line, and stops at the first directory holding neither `.done` nor `.blocked`. Run over the tree as it stands, that loop returns `workspace/volume-09/batch-0001`. **The condition this section named until the repair named above — that the walk would keep selecting `workspace/volume-08/volume-close/` until the runner wrote `.done` on it — resolved itself when the runner did, that directory holds `.done`, and the sentence is named here and deleted nowhere.** **The blind spot of that measurement is written beside its result: it reads the tree and not the selector's memory and it does not know what a previous run selected. The clause this one replaces, verbatim — *and it says nothing about the `.checkpoint` left in `workspace/volume-09/volume-09-outline/`, which is a runner artifact on a branch and not one of the three markers the walk looks for* — is false, there is no `.checkpoint` in this repository, and it is named here and deleted nowhere.** No phase may write a marker, because a phase that marks its own directory cannot be finished or retried by either selector. This repair wrote none.

## What is owed, and this phase discharged none of it

**The four debts, unchanged and restated in full, in the corrected wording: an owed review of Volume 04's Batch 0005, four volumes on; owed second readings of Volume 05's Batches 0003, 0004 and 0005 and of Volume 06's own Batch 0003, which is four and not three; the review gate, which opened and produced findings on all seven Batch 0005 phases the commit history records, and has fallen back to the writing agent every time it has been asked, and has never once produced a review that could be certified independent, and a gate that only ever falls back is not a gate that passed either; and the open items that are not plot, with the sentence bound among them.** **The number of debts has not moved in eight volumes and the number of phases that have claimed to discharge one is zero, and this phase is not among them.** A close is where a debt is most likely to be quietly dropped, because a close feels like a finish, and so is a handoff.

**The third debt has a third instance and it is item 89: no reviewer has read the close of Volume 08.** A close writes the volume's last word in five files that the next volume's writer reads first, so an unexamined close is not one unreviewed batch out of fifty, it is the thing every later writer inherits before anything else. The finding is not new — it is item 82, and item 43, and the archive's own note that the first header in `current-md-superseded.md` claimed an independent review that was not run — and it is new in that respect. **This phase is also unreviewed, and it wrote the files that plan Volume 09 will be built on, so the same debt now has a fourth instance and the count of instances is not a measure of the debt.**

**The bill at Lowcross stands at nineteen pounds three and fourpence, unpaid, nobody liable, and Volume 08 named it zero times in fifty files, which is five batches in a row and is a decision and not an oversight. The form that came through a letter slot in Chapter 0389 is a different thing, carries no figure, and the page does not say the two are the same debt.**

## The standing locks, in the short form a writer needs

**Nobody asks anybody anything out loud. A question mark in a mouth is punctuation and is not an asking, and the two counts are independent and both are printed; Volume 08's fifty files carry four question marks, one in each of Chapters 0364, 0373, 0375 and 0383, and not one of the four is an asking, and seven askings, which did not move, and the figure is printed in none of the fifty chapters. Nobody is thanked, forgiven or sent for, and nothing is resolved.** The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void. The question on the shelf stays a question with no full stop and its author is not asked a second time. The figure at the end of the cold passage is not handed on and gets no heading. The name at the end of a struck line is not printed and the name of the hand that struck it is not printed. The guarantee is not printed in its own words and no child is named in it. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are not asked one question about a number, and the man of about fifty-five with the chain and the man of about sixty-one are neither of them one of them. A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked, unsent for, and not going to start, and the girl is not given the chance to say no. **The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in this volume.**

**A man of about sixty-one, a woman of about twenty-six and a woman of twenty are three people and no two of them are ever in one room, and this volume put none of them together. A woman of about forty with a scuttle is a fourth person and is not the woman of about twenty-six. A clerk of about fifty-three and the man of about sixty-one are in the same building and are not in the same room in any of the last ten chapters. And a fourth separation, added by the repair of Batch 0005 and carrying item 29's standing instruction into a building nobody had thought to check: the woman who keeps the ground floor of the rented house is not the clerk of about fifty-three.** The three people the state layer keeps apart at that address are the clerk, the woman who keeps the ground floor, and Marek Kest, who is the only one of the three who has never given either of the other two his name. **A merge does not need two rooms to happen; it needs two people and one mouth, and no two of the three may ever be in one room and no chapter may state or deny a distance between any two of them. The last clause of that sentence is withdrawn by the repair that took `logs/batch-0001.review.log`, and it is named here and deleted nowhere: 0390 and 0399, both closed chapters, put the woman who keeps the ground floor and Marek Kest in one room, and 0406 states a distance between them, and the outline states the same distance itself, and the sentence is therefore false as it stands and cannot be obeyed by a writer who is also obeying the page. What holds, and what the repair verified by measurement, is the fourth separation as the outline names it — the woman who keeps the ground floor is not the clerk of about fifty-three — and the clerk of about fifty-three is in none of Volume 09's first ten chapters. The account is in the section headed *The fourth separation, the one finding not applied, and the page it rests on*.**

**The calendar, and the two things about it a Volume 09 writer must be handed rather than derive.** A month in this calendar is four weeks and the day inside the week is the inherited cycle of second, second, fourth, fourth, restarting with each month. **The sixth named year is the fifth with one more *after the* in it and the seventh is the sixth with one more, both written out in full at every occurrence and abbreviated nowhere; the seventh was added and not moved, it appears once in each of Chapters 0397 to 0400 and nowhere in the three hundred and ninety-six chapters before it, and that decision is recorded. The age sweep is therefore right there and wrong in 0381 and 0386, the surname sweep never touches the file at all, and the three chapters differ by nothing a string can see — only by what the man standing in the room says.** The count of chapters cannot see a scene, and a floor that is a number can be met by a sentence in somebody else's mouth.

**The ledger, by `grep -o -E '\*\*[0-9]{1,3}\. OPEN' state/open-threads.md | grep -o -E '[0-9]+' | sort -n -u | wc -l`: eighty-seven distinct item numbers, being items 1 to 48 and 51 to 89, measured on that file **before** this phase consolidated anything, and three after it, being items 43, 44 and 90, of which 43 and 44 stayed, with the other eighty-five in the `state/open-threads.md` block of `state/archive/rolling-volume-08-records.md`; items 49 and 50 are the only numbers absent from both files.** **The blind spot: this is a count of entries, the number everybody has been quoting is the highest number used, and the file that was counted has since been emptied into the archive by this same phase, so the figure that was printed had already drifted by the time this header was written and sat four files downstream of its own cause.** Sixty-three was quoted as entries and is not; eighty-nine is the high-water mark and is not a count; eighty-seven is the measured count of the rolling ledger before the eighth enforcement and is not what the live file returns now. **A figure quoted without the state of the object it was measured on has already drifted, and the consolidation that made the archive correct did not update the sentence that reported the file it emptied.** Item 43 is a debt and not a figure and it may not be repaired.

**And the blind spot of every check this project owns, written beside its results because a check that returns zero is evidence of nothing until the shape of damage it is blind to has been checked.** A window asks whether two files agree, and a reprint agrees with everything, so **every governing figure in this header is clean on a page that carried, through a full batch of ten drafts and two reading passes, thirty-seven re-printed identification and room-description passages, two weekday names, a duplicated emphasis marker pair, three pieces of card language in narration and nine sentences over ninety words, and the twenty-word paragraph sweep saw none of the thirty-seven while the twelve-word test saw all of them.** A denominator is a choice and its column is a choice. A count of `about` cannot tell a hedge from a preposition. **And the one this phase turned up rather than confirmed: the check that reads a protagonist's presence off a string is a check that cannot see a person, and it returned an eighteen where the answer is eleven, and it was wrong by exactly the seven files that carry one of the two strings without carrying him, and it would have done so for every volume, and nobody had run it before because a count of a name is a count of a name.** Write every blind spot beside its result, measure every bound after the last edit with the method stated, name the phase that made any repair, and **never call a self-audit, a second pass, a close or a repair a review.**

**The six rolling files are not reconciled in this header, and the standing rule that replaces the reconciliation is the one the close set: a total that moves every time any of its six files is edited is measured after the last edit with the method stated, and it is printed once, in one file, in one place, in one form, and never here.** It is at the foot of this phase's section in `state/batch-summary.md`.

# VOLUME 09 BATCH 0003, CHAPTERS 0421 TO 0430, MOVEMENT THREE, THE TURN — A BLANK IS FILLED IN AND THE COUNT DOES NOT MOVE

*Appended downward by the phase that took `workspace/volume-09/batch-0003/PROMPT.md`. **Nothing above this point is rewritten and no status about any person above is changed.** This batch wrote ten files into `chapters/volume-09/`, opened no chapter of any closed volume, edited no file in `outline/`, named no controller file, and wrote no marker in its own directory. **It is a chapter batch and it is not a review, not a self-audit, not a second reading, not a close and not a repair, and nothing in this file reports itself as one. It discharged none of the four debts.**

## The turn, and it is on the page in a mouth and not in a record

**In 0423 a young man from the shipping floor put fourpence on the boards at the top of four flights, was handed a piece of paper with nothing printed on it out of the case at the near end, and filled it in by hand in about a minute and a half with a stub of pencil, and folded it in three and put it inside his coat and buttoned the coat over it and went down the four flights.** He is not a villain, he has no plan, he is on no list in this matter, and nothing was asked of him and he said nothing to anybody. He said two things out loud into a room that had given him nothing to say them to, and neither was addressed to a person and neither was picked up: **"Everything with a heading on it has somewhere to go"** and **"This has not got one."** That is the whole of the turn and it is nine words and it is in a mouth.

**The count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven and it was seven before this batch and seven after it, and the reason is the page's own definition and not this batch's decision: an asking is a thing put to a person out loud in a room by somebody who wants a thing out of the answer, and a blank filled in at a counter is a person putting a thing to a column, and a column cannot be hurt by what comes back.** The person who filled it in has not been heard by anybody. Fourpence went into the ordinary place and the paper did not go anywhere that anybody in that room could account for. **What is written on the piece of paper is printed in no chapter of this volume and may not be printed in any of them, and no chapter in these ten says what it is.**

## The three contradictions the movement was required to contain, and where each one is

**A woman of twenty-four who sees it happen and cannot say anything about it and is not going to.** 0423, in a pair of hands a man can see across a counter, saying nothing. 0424, a week later, the point of view: she is twenty minutes early again after having stopped in 0418, and Marn Ottery names the fact as a fact and refuses to ask her about it, and she says one word about what she saw and that word is *no*, and she is not asked for a word and is not thanked. **Her undertaking is live, unretired and unexercised and its date is not said out loud in any of the ten chapters and is not said out loud in this state record either.** The decision about whether she trusts a colleague's judgment is put into the room in 0424 and refused in the room and is still unmade.

**A young man who is right out loud, twice, about what has just happened, in about nine words, and is stopped both times.** 0425. *No column means no place to put a person*, said to a shut door, and *It cannot be filed and it cannot be put on me*, said to a woman on a step. **He is stopped once by Marek Kest, who will not hear the same true thing twice in one week and says so to a door and does not soften it, and once by the woman who keeps the ground floor, who has a thing of her own in that house that nobody gave her and who is not going to be handed a second one off a stranger in a street at the fifth hour. Neither stop is unkind and neither stop takes the thing back out of the two people it has already been said to, and that is the finding and it is not the young man's fault.** He is not a villain, nobody thanked him, and he is not on any list.

**And the chapter the outline asks for, the one in which somebody is asked nothing and says a true thing anyway, and it costs.** 0428. The woman who keeps the ground floor of a rented house, about twenty years at the bottom of a stranger's stairs, alone, at the fifth hour, says out loud to an empty room that she has known for nine years what the man she takes rent from is, and has said nothing to anybody about it for nine years, and chose it, and that she chose it nine times a year with her own two hands. **There is a tin behind the boiler with nine years of his rent in it in coin and she has never counted it and there is no reason to count it, and the arrangement that made that floor the cheapest in the city is that nobody in that house can be shown anything, and a true thing said out loud in a house is a thing the house can be shown.** She cannot take it back. Nobody will thank her. Nobody sends for her. She does not go up those stairs. **And she does not move the tin, and the reason is that moving it is a sensible thing to do, and a sensible thing done on purpose is a thing a person can be shown doing, and she is not going to spend twenty years on a boiler.** She is not the clerk of about fifty-three, has never been in that building, and does not know what was said in it.

## The decision this batch took that no card told it to take, and it is Movement Four's opening

**The filled-in sheet does not arrive at the second hand's floor in this batch.** Card 0427 gave the choice: it either comes or it does not, and if it does it has to arrive as an ordinary thing and be signed at the foot like the other four hundred. **It does not, and 0427 says why in a mouth rather than in a record: a thing with no column does not travel to a floor with a man at the foot of about four hundred sheets a year on it, it travels to a coat, and the coat is on a back, and the back is the cheapest party in this matter.** So in 0427 the man of about sixty-one gives a third answer to his pen pot, and it is not either of the two he has given before, and the sentence is that in nineteen years the first thing that would have come up that stair wanting nothing off him did not come. The hook was empty inside a minute. **The next movement has to open with a sheet with no column arriving, and this batch has put the reason it did not arrive in a man's mouth, and the reason is a price and not a decision.**

## What this batch found about its own instruments, and two of the three are about the instruments being wrong

**One, a batch can repeat itself and a paragraph sweep run only against closed files cannot see it.** Four chapters of this batch open at the counter at the top of four flights, being 0422, 0423, 0424 and 0430, and the first draft of all four opened with the same twenty words about the same case, the same box and the same drawer. The twenty-word window caught it only when it was run over the ten files as well as against the closed page, and **the window's usual scope is the closed page, and a volume's most-used room is where a batch will repeat itself first.** All four now open on different furniture and none of them describes the room.
**Two, the classifier that sorts a window hit into formula or prose has to strip punctuation, and a splitter has to allow a closing quotation mark between the full stop and the space.** The first classifier reported 24 of 105 date lines as prose because `next,` fell out of the date vocabulary. The first splitter reported a maximum sentence of 239 words where the real maximum is 87, because a rule requiring whitespace immediately after a full stop swallows every closing quotation mark. **Both errors ran in the same direction, reporting the page as worse than it is, and neither is visible to a count.** The correct figures are in the figures section above and the wrong ones are named there and are not deleted.
**Three, and this is the standing the batch inherited and confirmed: a state record that describes the repository is a record about the world and not about the page, and nothing in this project checks the world.** The two false premises this prompt carried about markers and checkpoints were both inherited from `state/current.md` and were caught on the tree and in the git history and not by reading a chapter.

## The protagonist's floor, by reading and not by a string, with the sentences printed

**Three chapters, 0422, 0425 and 0428, in person in two of the three, want visible in one.** The floor for a movement is three, in person in two, want visible in one, and it is met exactly. The sentence that puts him in each room is in the floor section above and is not repeated here. **Both sweeps return one file and the answer is three, and the reason is the reason Volume 08's were wrong about seven: in 0422 and 0428 he is in the room, or in the cost of the room, and is named in neither and given no age in neither.** He holds nothing at the end of the batch that he held at the start. He is not thanked, nobody asked him anything, his reason for not reaching a stage is paid a second time zero times, and he is not a carrier and nothing in 0425 made him one.

# THE REPAIR OF VOLUME 09 BATCH 0004 — WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND, WHAT WAS CHANGED, AND THE STANDING IT ADDS

*Appended downward by the phase that took `logs/batch-0004.review.log`. **Nothing above this point is rewritten and no status about any person above is changed. It is a repair and not a batch, not a self-audit, not a second reading, not a close and not a review, because the review gate fell back to the writing agent and the writing agent read its own work. It discharged none of the four debts.** Five chapters were edited: 0431, 0432, 0434, 0435 and 0440. No closed chapter was opened, no file in `outline/` was edited, no controller file was touched, and no marker was written in any directory.

## The six findings, one line each, and the seventh the review did not make

1. **A lock, in the chapters: two weekday names.** *Tuesday* and *Wednesday*, at the old `chapter-0432.md:33` and `chapter-0440.md:21`, against a prompt that forbids a weekday name in anything it writes, and the only two in forty files. **Out of the page.**
2. **The state layer denied finding one**, in the section whose own headline is that a state record which does not reproduce against its page is a premise and not a measurement. **Corrected in place, the wrong sentence quoted beside the right one, deleted nowhere.**
3. **A count that was not made to fit.** 0431 claimed nine words over thirteen, and the state layer added twenty-two for a sentence of twenty-five and once gave the same sentence as both nine and twenty-two. **The sentence was changed and not the count, because the nine-word motif is inherited from 0425 and is load-bearing in four other chapters.**
4. **Two elapsed figures in 0435 that the calendar does not support.** Three weeks is five. Seven weeks is **eleven**, and the review's own referent was wrong: in 0430 the clerk spoke and the thing counted is her writing none of it down, which is first in 0424.
5. **A sweep row that returns nothing when run.** `House` case-sensitive is **zero files**; the two files named are lowercase `house` and both are the ordinary noun for a building.
6. **A floor only the state record could see.** The protagonist is claimed in person in two of three chapters, and 0440 identified nobody, so the in-person half rested on a record asserting something the page did not say. **The page was changed instead of the record, and the floor is now met by reading.**
7. **Not in the review, and this repair's most confident finding: 0434 dated a counter visit four months ago and the calendar gives twenty-seven weeks**, and 0413 calls the same visit six weeks. It is about six months. **Three elapsed figures in ten chapters, two caught and one missed, and the missed one is the same class as the two that were caught.**

## What the repair did not do, and each of those is a decision and not an omission

**It did not weaken the state record where the record was right.** Finding six could have been closed by deleting the floor claim and recording that the movement is short. **It was not, because the floor is in the outline of record and a chapter can be made to carry it, and the reason the state record could not be trusted is that nobody had opened the file.**

**It did not take a figure from the review.** The review supplied five weeks for the second elapsed figure and five is wrong. **The repair measured it, got eleven, and wrote eleven, and a repair that had trusted its reviewer would have put a wrong number into a chapter with a citation attached to it.**

**It did not restart the batch and did not rewrite the five chapters.** Nine words and one paragraph across ten finished chapters, and the prose that was there is the prose that is there now, and the one paragraph added was written to be the man of 0407 rather than to be good.

**It did not develop anything.** No want moved, no thread closed, no name printed, no stage reached, no office given, no form drawn, and the count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven and is seven before the repair and is seven after it.

## The standing this repair adds, and it is the first one in this project that is about a lock and not about a check

**A lock is a thing this project asserts about itself, and the assertion is the only part of the record with no instrument attached to it.** Every other finding in three batches has been about the shape of a check: a classifier that was lexical and not positional, a reconciliation that was consistent and not accurate, a count of question marks that was blind to an asking. **This one is a lock that was written down as held, in a prompt, in a state file, in a batch summary and in four places across the record, and it was broken twice in the batch the prompt sent, and both breaches were found by running a sweep and neither was found by reading a chapter.** A weekday name is two words in a sentence and a reader does not stop on it, and a prompt that says a thing is not a thing may not happen is a rule and not a check, and this project has eight volumes of rules it calls checks.

# VOLUME 09 BATCH 0005, CHAPTERS 0441 TO 0450, MOVEMENT FIVE, THE CLIMAX — it is a chapter batch and not a review, not a self-audit, not a second reading, not a close and not a repair, and it discharged none of the four debts, and it created one next phase and it is the close of the volume

## The state of the novel, in one paragraph, after Chapter 0450

A box of about four hundred blanks that stood under the far end of nine foot of deal at the top of four flights for eleven years came out in nine minutes and went down four flights and about four miles in the two hands of a man who is paid for a corner and not for a page, and was set down on the floor of a room on a second floor and was not opened. In the last week of the seventh named year a man of about sixty-one signed the same sheet twice and found out nothing. In the fourth week of the first month of the eighth named year a man went up a stair in a rented house who is not the man whose rent it is, and the woman at the bottom of those stairs did not follow him and refused him a name. In the first week of the second month a piece of paper with nothing printed on it was put on a table in the room taken by the week by a man who could not say where he got it and did not knock, and nobody sent it, and a week later it was stood against the base of about four feet of bare wall where it can be seen, and it is not on a form and it is not in a book and it is not a record. In the third week of the same month a woman of twenty-four worked out that a person with something behind her is not available and told nobody. In the last chapter of the volume the man who brought the paper came back with nothing in his hands and said he is not going to come a third time, because a man who goes to a door twice has got a habit and a habit is the only thing about a man that anybody can be shown. **Nobody in nine volumes has been thanked, nobody has been forgiven, nobody has been sent for, and nothing has been resolved, and the arrangement is still standing.**

## Who is alive, who wants what, and what each of them is refused, after Chapter 0450

**Marek Kest, thirty-eight.** Wants the erased name of his mother and the disputed family claim, and the name is not printed in any chapter of this volume and the hand that struck the line is not printed either. He has a piece of paper with nothing printed on it standing against the base of four feet of bare wall that has been bare for two years, and the space at the foot of a sheet is the exact width of a name and nothing is written in it. He holds nothing, refused the reading, did not exercise the thing he is able to exercise, reached no stage, and was given a second copy of nothing. He was thanked by nobody.

**Tamsin Rook, twenty-four.** Has worked out what she has been standing ready for, which is a box of about four hundred pieces of paper nobody can account for, and has worked out that a person with something behind her is not available, and has said neither out loud to anybody. Not an organiser, not a clerk with a title, not a person somebody has finally asked, not a person anybody has made a decision about. Her undertaking is live, unretired and unexercised and its date is not said out loud anywhere. The decision about whether she takes her colleague's judgment is unmade.

**Marn Ottery, thirty-four, eleven years at those boards.** Had the box moved, said out loud before it was moved that a clerk who moves a box is a clerk who has made a statement about it, and refused to say in that room that she wished it out of there before the month began. Not thanked. The box is not the supply and she said so on the page in 0410 and it is not contradicted. The drawer is shut and two of the four things in it have never been opened and the fourth item on that board is still the one none of the three clerks can account for.

**The man of about twenty-six who is paid by the corner.** Carried the box four miles and a piece of paper to a door, told nobody where the paper came from, said out loud going down a stair that he is not going to be findable, and said he is not going to be thanked. He is the cheapest party in this matter and the cost is exact and it is paid in him. **He is never in one room with the young man from the shipping floor and neither is described with the other's noun, and the disagreement inside closed Chapter 0396 about his gender is carried unrepaired on purpose.**

**The man of about sixty-one.** Signed a sheet twice in the last week of the seventh named year and found out nothing, and that is the first thing he has had to carry that is not a number, and there is no pot on that sill for it. About nine of about nine hundred a year are still not what the person above him wrote and he signed them all and is still the only person alive who knows which and cannot write one down. He is not one of the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph and never is. Nobody sent for him and nobody thanked him.

**Halla Wray, fifty-one.** Stood at the open side of a shed and let a stranger look at two people she could have refused him, having been told what that would cost, and the cost was not paid and was not asked about. The second half of a sentence she began in a doorway has still not arrived and nobody asked her for it.

**The woman of twenty at the counting room at the back of a dye end.** Had the answer to a stranger's question about a book and did not give it, and the man from the front office refused to write a lot number and was right. Sixteen volumes, fifteen out on loan, the sixteenth with her own name in capitals at the head of it and unopened. The wage of nineteen days of a crew's money is in a coat about four miles off and the paper in that pocket with a printed ruled space on the back of it is still clean. Not paid, not sent for, not thanked, not forgiven.

**The woman who keeps the ground floor of a rented house.** Watched a man go up four steps who is not the man whose rent it is and did not follow him and refused him a name, and the change in that house was made by somebody other than her and not at her asking and she cannot put it back. She has never gone up those stairs in about twenty years and is never going to. The tin is behind the boiler and she has not counted it.

**The man of about thirty-four with a fair hand.** Came to that room a second time with nothing in his hands and said before he was asked that he is not going to be the man who takes the paper. The number in his head is not in the room and was neither confirmed nor denied. **The next asking is his and is nobody's yet and this volume did not make it anybody's.**

## What runs

**A box of about four hundred blanks, four miles off, unopened, in a room on a second floor, against a wall that has nothing on it.** **A piece of paper with nothing printed on it, standing against the base of a bare wall in a room taken by the week, where he can see it.** A second mark on a sheet in a corridor nine miles off, under a hand that cannot read a paragraph, and nobody told him. A practice in two people about four hundred and thirty miles apart with no list, no form, no heading and no fund. A form with a printed heading over a ruled space that came through a letter slot about two years ago and was not returned. A question on a shelf under a window with no pane in it, with a name at the foot of it and no full stop. Nine books out of a shed at the end of a lane and a form on a board by the door that nobody in that lane reads. A set of days at a counter between 0449 and 0450 that nobody will describe. **The count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven, and the next asking is nobody's yet.**

**One, the finding, and it is not a figure.** The batch printed the twenty-word window as **0 prose, 0 prose, 0 prose** in this file, in `state/batch-summary.md` and in §Three of `workspace/volume-09/volume-close/PROMPT.md`, with a positive control that fires, **and it was false.** The true figures are **4, 18 and 0** and **3, 38 and 0** under the two tokenizers, and the largest single prose re-print was **23 consecutive identical words between 0441 and 0449**, the counter's closing ritual in the same words in two chapters of one batch, **and the batch's own record names the fix for that run in a sentence about stale word counts and the fix was never made.** The cause is not the classifier's logic and is the formula list: it had **eight entries and it needed twenty**, and **a classifier whose list is too short does not report prose for the formulas it is missing, it reports zero, and a zero with a working control is the most convincing result this project's instruments can produce and the least informative.**

**Two, the instrument finding that makes the first one general.** **A control tests the instrument against something the instrument already knows, and a list's own contents are something the instrument knows by construction, so a control planted on a formula the list contains confirms the mechanism and not the coverage — and the coverage was the whole of what was wrong.** The standing this adds: **when a list is the thing doing the classifying, the control has to be drawn from outside the list, or the control is a test of the list and not of the page.** The missing nine were found by measuring the volume's known formulas by hand against the classifier and not by the control.

**Three, the second instrument defect, in this repair's own code.** The filter keeping a section break out of the prose bucket was written as `if '--' in tokens` where `tokens` is a list — a list-membership test where a substring test was meant, **silently always false, firing on nothing across two full runs** and admitting two identical internal hits that were visibly a `---` followed by a sentence. **A filter which never fires does not announce itself, does not throw, and produces a figure that looks exactly like a finding.**

# THE VOLUME 10 OUTLINE OF RECORD: WHAT WAS WRITTEN, WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND TWO FIGURES THAT CORRECT A RECORD

*Written by the phase that took `workspace/volume-10/volume-10-outline/PROMPT.md`. **A plan and not a review, a self-audit, a second reading, a close or a repair. No line of the novel was written, no chapter file opened for edit, nothing resolved, nobody thanked, forgiven or sent for, and none of the four debts discharged. It wrote no marker in its own directory, and it created exactly one next phase, `workspace/volume-10/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`, at the end of the run and by then its own file was closed.** `outline/volume-10.md` is the outline of record for Chapters 0451 to 0500, is titled *The Second Sheet*, is 143,130 bytes across 351 lines, and **is closed the moment it was written; no phase after the one that wrote it may edit a line of it, amend it above its closing section, correct it in place or append to it.** Every figure below was measured by this phase with the method named beside it. Every superseded figure is named and deleted nowhere. The one next phase is Batch 0001 and no other exists.*

**One, the volume in three sentences, because a cold reader needs the shape before the fields.** Volume 10 is the volume in which a piece of paper gets a second holder. **A copy is the only object in this empire that can be made twice and still be honest, it is the only object a person can be given instead of the thing they came for, and a thing anybody may have cannot be recalled, and that is the only instrument anybody in this matter has ever had — and it has been used once in nine volumes, at fourpence, in a room at the top of a stair, and the second use is in this volume and is not a safety and is not a witness.** The volume's answer to the question the last volume handed on is that the size of a thing is not the number of sheets in it but the number of people it can be taken off, and a thing with one holder is a person and a thing with two is a record, and **this matter has run for nine volumes on the first and has never once had the second.** The turn is declared in Movement Three and the climax in Movement Five, and both were declared by name in advance for the reason the last volume's outline gives, which is that a plan that is right twice is not thereby right a third time and the tenth declared position is always the one the page has already contradicted somewhere nobody looked.

**Two, what the plan's block gives Volume 10 and what the page has, measured, and the count of the block is the title and ten fields and the count is right.** Read at a word boundary over all 450 closed chapter files, `emberroot`, `coalition`, `charter`, `mountain`, `vault`, `quorum` and `recover` all return **zero files and zero occurrences**, and `emberroot` returns zero as a case-insensitive substring as well; `Architect`, `ratify`, `ratification` and `subvert` return zero. `compact` returns **two**, and one of the two is a man's mouth saying he has never seen it. `convocation` returns **two**, and both are the same sentence inside a quoted instrument in Volume 02, and a convocation has never been called. `Crown Kiln` returns **31 across 24 files and every one is in Volume 01 or Volume 02, the last at Chapter 0099**, so the plan's place is real and has been off the page for eight volumes. `Cinder Clause` returns **one**, in one file, said once in Chapter 0197 and then stopped. `Seryn` 2 in 2 files, `Vaunt` 19 in 3, `Pell` 125 in 17 — **so three of the plan's six "factions" are people the page has already put somewhere, and a page person is not a faction.** `House` as a case-insensitive substring is 2,069 across the 450 files and **2,011 of those are in the closed four hundred, which reproduces the figure `outline/volume-09.md` printed exactly and on that reading only**; case-sensitively at a word boundary it is 131 across 35 files and none of them is in a chapter's prose. The block's power-and-relationship field is refused hardest and its figure is zero: **`Architect` is zero across four hundred and fifty chapters, he is not at a stage and is not going to arrive at one, and no romance has begun in nine volumes and the ending of record puts that arc in Volume 12 at a hearing and it is not paid early and not refused.**

**Three, THE FIRST CORRECTION, and it corrects a record rather than confirming it, and it is a year name inside a longer year name.** The handoff that wrote this phase's prompt printed the sixth named year's name on **forty-five** date lines, being Chapters 0351 to 0396, and **ninety-nine files** bounded to files rather than lines. # VOLUME 10 BATCH 0001, CHAPTERS 0451 TO 0460, MOVEMENT ONE — THE SEED, AND WHAT YOU GET FOR THE FOURPENCE

*Written by the phase that took `workspace/volume-10/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`, after a checkpoint at which the ten chapters existed and this state layer had never been written. **It is a chapter batch and not a review, not a self-audit, not a second reading, not a close and not a repair, and it discharged none of the four debts.** `outline/volume-10.md` is closed, was read in the order that file asks to be read in, and was not opened for edit. **A batch is not a close: Chapter 0460 is the last chapter of the batch and not of the volume, and this batch writes no last line of any volume.** The plan's title is not used anywhere and no file this phase wrote prints the word the plan's title is built on.*

## The state of the novel, in one paragraph, after Chapter 0460

A volume in which a piece of paper gets a second holder has opened, and the first ten weeks have put the copy on the page as a made object with a maker, a price of fourpence, a time cost of about ninety seconds and a queue, and as a substitute — what you get for the fourpence and not what you came for. There is a printed strip along the top of every blank that counter has ever sold, the strip is the same strip, the four things printed along the top of it are the same four things, and there is a knife in a drawer there that takes about four seconds to cut a line into it if a person wants one cut; **nobody in these ten chapters cuts one, the drawer is not opened, and nothing this batch writes says whether the drawer the knife is in is the drawer under the board, because the page does not say and a chapter that says so is inventing a fact about a shut drawer.** The three unaccounted objects in that one room are all still shut and all still unaccounted for: about four hundred bought and unfilled blanks under the far end of the boards that are not the supply, a drawer shut for eleven years with four things in it of which two have never been opened, and a fourth item on a board carrying four items and not one of them time, in Marn Ottery's own hand, about four years old, put there by herself, and **named in this movement and resolved in none of its five.** A woman of twenty-four has worked out that a copy is the only object in that room that can be bought twice, by watching two people pay fourpence for the same object in one morning, and has said none of it out loud; a clerk of about twenty-nine has worked out that a line cut into a printed strip would be a mark with no column over it and therefore could not be laid against anybody, and has said that once and will not say a second thing; a woman of twenty-six at the lock end of about four hundred yards of cold flags has a figure on no paper that has gone up and does not get a heading and has said the protagonist's name out loud once to the flags; a man of about twenty-six paid by the corner has come up those four flights twice in ten chapters, put nothing down either time, and been given no decision. **And a man of thirty-eight has been up those four flights four times in his life, put nothing on those boards on any of them, and is going down them with two sheets in a coat that he has told nobody about and is not going to tell anybody about this volume, and one of those two sheets is a copy he bought for fourpence about two years ago and the other is a leaf with a name struck out of it by a hand that was not his mother's.** Nobody is thanked, nobody is forgiven, nobody is sent for, nothing is resolved, and the arrangement is still standing.

## What runs

The copy as an instrument, on a queue, at fourpence, made in about ninety seconds by a clerk who is not thanked for it. Three unaccounted objects in one room, none of them with a form. A printed strip that would carry an identical mark on every sheet that counter sells. A woman's readiness, live and unretired and unexercised, and the twenty minutes before the hour that are not a decision. A class that can be re-entered by whoever fills in the next form. About nine hundred sheets a year signed at the foot by a man who cannot read a paragraph, of which about nine are not what the person above him wrote and none of the nine is on anything. A second mark on one sheet that nobody can point at. A figure on no paper that has gone up. Two sheets in one coat on opposite sides. A box at the end of a shipping floor that has not moved for about nineteen years, and a statement made twice to one woman, where the batch's first draft put two people in a yard and a review found the closed page gives one hearer.

### Who is alive, who wants what, and what each of them is refused

**Marek Kest, thirty-eight, the protagonist, on the page in four chapters of this movement and in person in two of them — 0461, 0463, 0465 and 0467 — and his want visible in two, 0461 and 0463.** Counted by reading, with the sentence in each room printed in the batch summary and the continuity record, because a count is not an answer to a floor. **He holds nothing and was given nothing: no office, no fund, no list, no leave, no post, no commission, no warrant, no certification, no heading over his name, no second copy of anything, no stage, and no reading and no exercise of the thing he is able to do. ### The standing locks, in the short form a writer needs, and every one of them held in all ten files

The first lock is that nobody asks anybody anything out loud, **and a check that looks for that with a question mark does not find it: a question mark is punctuation and an asking is a thing put to a person out loud by somebody who wants a thing out of the answer, and the two counts are independent, and this batch carried zero question marks and drafted two askings and caught both by reading the ten files.** The two are at 0469, where a woman at her own door told a man to say it, and at 0462, where a clerk was told she could write a thing down; both are out, and both would have been the eighth in this matter, and the state row that reports this batch clean was written after the repairs and not before them, which is the tenth time that has happened in this project and is item 118. and `outline/volume-02.md` still assigned Corvin Dray's sentence and Tamsin Rook's appointment to Chapters 91–100 when the sentence is Chapter 65 and the appointment is a conversion of a holding she has had since the eleventh of the ninth month, and its midpoint-reversal card still described a Lowcross file that Chapter 58 has already delivered. **(7) Four findings are recorded here and are NOT actioned, because the files are controller-owned and this pass may not touch them:** `opencode run --agent novel-reviewer` in `scripts/novel_runner.sh:245` cannot work while `.opencode/agent/novel-reviewer.md` declares `mode: subagent`, so the review phase silently runs the writer and **there is no independent reviewer anywhere in the review-to-fix loop for any batch in this repository**; the same bad flag is at `.github/workflows/*.yml:64`. `state/phase-ledger.json` is about sixty chapters stale, is read by nothing, and is declared permanently stale in `state/current.md`. `workspace/volume-02/batch-0001/` does not exist, and it must not be created by a writing phase, because a prompt directory without a `.done` marker sorts ahead of `batch-0002` and the dispatcher would run it as a duplicate phase; the batch is traceable through `outline/batches/volume-02-batch-0001.md` and this file instead. And `workspace/continuation/next/` still has no `.done` and shadows `workspace/volume-02/batch-0002/` until the current run finishes. **None of these four is a fiction defect and none was worked around.**

**The twenty-two internal contradictions, each repaired at the line and each verifiable in the file named.**

1. **Ch 51, the room counted three ways.** Nine bundles and four loose objects is thirteen things, and the chapter said he counted the room twice and got nine. He now counts **the bundles** twice. The 440 chased documents no longer sit *four feet from his own table*, which was the Ashfall bundle's own distance and was making two facts out of one; they are in a tray on the sill.
2. **Ch 51, a garbled clause.** *He had been transferred into a chair that is the reason a document cannot be got at by asking* is now *He had been transferred to a counter, and a counter is a place a document comes to and not a place a person goes to ask for one*, which is what the next paragraph says.
3. **Ch 52, a non-sequitur.** *Twice is eighty-two and once is forty-one, and I have never once been able to make that come out the same way twice* was both a non-sequitur and a contradiction of the line above it. It is now the count holding steady, and her joke is that this is the first time.
4. **Ch 52, the register page.** The two gaps are **on two pages, not one** — the twelfth of the ninth month of last year and the sixth of the fourth month of this year — and the page now says so, which also agrees with Chapter 55, where Marrow turns the register to *the page for last year and the page for this year*.
5. **Ch 52 and Ch 55, a duplicated clause inside Marek's own page** (*a finding about the reader, and it is a finding about a reader*) is cut.
6. **Ch 53, three cycles of fifty-four.** The line read as 162. It is now *Three cycles and fifty-four filed copies*, and the 31/54/60 arithmetic in divergence five holds on the page as well as in the card.
7. **Ch 53, a wall dated after it was read.** The outgoing-rack paragraph was dated the fourth of the tenth month and the man from the works read the wall on the second of the tenth. It is now the **twenty-eighth of the ninth month**, which also stops it colliding with the fourth of the tenth, which is Volume 01's Sallow date and belongs to that line alone.
8. **Ch 54, the same copyist at two ages.** A woman of twenty wrote the four questions nine weeks earlier; the copyist who comes to the table with four pence of carriage is a copyist of about forty. She is now **a woman of about forty**, the same person, which is the point of the paragraph.
9. **Ch 54, nine weeks and eleven weeks in one chapter.** The form comes back in about nine weeks and the girl reaches her finding in nine weeks; the wall note said eleven. It is now nine.
10. **Ch 55, four names a decade.** Marrow says fourteen a year, which over thirty years is four hundred and something, and then says he has about four names a decade. It is now **about a hundred and forty names a decade**.
11. **Ch 55, inverted causality.** *There were two gaps in it, because Tamsin Rook had filled them in* is now *there was not a gap in either of them, because she had filled both in*.
12. **Ch 55, eleven weeks that were four.** The letter is the seventeenth of the **tenth** month and the visit is the third week of the **eleventh**, which is four weeks, and the Docket could not have written before the fifteenth of the ninth because that is when Tamsin's card told it. **Four weeks** throughout, and the first week instead of the first fortnight. The Batch 0002 prompt now carries the letter, the four weeks, the fifteenth of the ninth and the two pages as locks.
13. **Ch 55, a headcount used as a count.** *Four hundred and eleven crossings a week* — 411 is the number of **people** on the far side of the Weir Cut in Chapter 54 and the crossings figure is 388. Marek's page now uses **three hundred and eighty-eight crossings**, and the Batch 0002 prompt states that the two are different figures and may not be swapped.
14. **Ch 56, the levy arithmetic.** Two pounds five and a farthing a quarter on four houses is **eight pounds and a penny a quarter**, and four of those is **thirty-two pounds and fourpence**, not nine pounds a quarter and thirty-six. Roke's line read aloud now says the true figures, and the farthing is still Nery Caudle's own money out of a cloth.
15. **Ch 56, five months called eleven.** The four questions went on a stone in the sixth month and the levy was read on the eleventh of the eleventh, so *the only paper in eleven months that the four questions have made better* is now **five months**, which is the same figure the letter to Marek uses two days later.
16. **Ch 57, nine paragraphs that are seven.** *Nine paragraphs, four of them about a printed sentence, one… one… and one* is **seven**, and the afternoon of the hearing is now counted correctly.
17. **Ch 59, nineteen years of arithmetic against a nine-year cycle.** The cost is nineteen pounds three and fourpence every nine years, and the chapter then accounted for nineteen years as four lots of a pound and fifteen lots of a pound. It is now **two repairs in nineteen years and about a pound a year in the years between**, and the fund is **about six pounds** on the average of four quarters against the six pounds and eightpence committed for the quarter, which is the figure everywhere else.
18. **Ch 58, the author arguing with continuity in the prose.** *no, that was Mosswake's, and this was a different building* is cut and the sentence stands on its own.
19. **Ch 58, three copies and four destinations.** The order was Crane, Sowle, Sarn, and then a rationale that named Marek second, and a dangling *that* in the third. The three copies are now Crane, Sowle, Sarn in that order, the rationale says the household first and Marek before he knew, and the dangling clause is gone.
20. **Ch 58, an eighth hour and a fourth hour.** The chapter put the third copy on Marek's table at the fourth hour and then said the cart went at the eighth hour at night. It is the **eighth hour of that night** throughout, which is what this file's chronology already said.
21. **Ch 60, five columns of which one was a price.** The fifth heading was *A shilling a copy*, which is a price and not a column, and the chapter then entered *four of the five columns out of five* and listed four items that matched none of the named columns. The headings are now **Date. Household. Duty. Next review. Copy sold**, the fourth is named as the one she could not fill, the second column is named as where the name and the door go, and Chapter 53's description of the form was brought into line.
22. **Ch 60, three garbled clauses and a date.** *A sentence she has now heard a man in a good coat's building say out loud* is now *a man in a good coat say out loud*; the long sentence beginning *which is the half of it that was the whole of the reason* is broken into four and the self-cancelling clause is cut, and *a man in a book is a thing that can be done in six months* is kept because it is the point; and **Corvin Dray's plea was read back and not refused again on the eighteenth of the ninth, the same afternoon**, not in the seventh month.

**And the meta-language breaches, which `AGENTS.md` forbids and which a repair pass on Batch 0004 already once caught.** Five narrator lines named the volume or the book and are now in-world: Chapter 51's *the only document of the whole of Volume 02 that he writes in the first week that nobody has asked him to write* and Chapter 55's *the only document of the whole of Volume 02 that he writes in a room with another person in it* — the same construction twice, which is why it was obvious; Chapter 57's *the most honest piece of paper any office in this book has produced*; Chapter 52's *Nobody in this book can reach a private book*; and Chapter 54's *the water holder is not named on any page of this*. Chapter 55's *I have never been in this book* is the register and is left alone. **The real tics the reviewer found instead of the blacklisted ones are the copula assertion and the number eleven**, and both were worked at without being allowed to become censorship: *and it is* is down from about seventy-one to sixty-five, *that is the* from about seventy to nineteen, and *about eleven \<unit\>* from six chapters to three, with the load-bearing elevens — the eleven protected people, the sixty-one certificates, the thirty-eight lines, the eleven lines on a schedule, the eleven months, and the **eleven weeks of unpaid labour on a bridge that is carried back on the twenty-fourth of the twelfth for an application in the first week of the fourth** — all left exactly as they are, and `counted` was reintroduced once in Chapter 51 because the manuscript's subject is counting and the word is doing work there.

## The Word-Count Record, Measured At The Volume 01 Close

**The command, so that every number here can be checked.** For each chapter, from the repository root:

`sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' chapters/volume-01/chapter-00NN.md | wc -w`

**Two counts exist in this project's history, they do not agree, and only one of them is reproducible.** Earlier phases reported **7,944 for Chapter 10** and **7,007 for Chapter 20**, with batch totals of **43,815** (Batch 0001) and **50,028** (Batch 0002), and described that count as prose-only with headings and scene-break rules excluded. **That description cannot be right**, because all four of those figures are *larger* than the command's, and an excluded-heading count would be smaller; the differences are also not a constant per chapter, so no single convention accounts for them. **The cause is not established and is not guessed at here.** What is established is that the command above is the measuring method this project named, that it is reproducible from the files as they stand, and that **it governs. Chapter 10 is 7,919 and Chapter 20 is 6,986.** The prose is identical under either convention; only the arithmetic of the count is in question.
