## Custody And Document Chain After Batch 0001

- **Where the source leaf lives.** The Venn source leaf is in the locked cabinet of the Notaries' Table at Auremar, along the north wall of the third gallery, and the key is on a chain around the neck of whichever supervisor is on duty. A certified packet sent to a district court carries the witness copy, not the leaf. This is canon and must not be contradicted: a district court has no power to open that cabinet, and a junior clerk's written comparison request cannot produce a leaf, because a comparison cannot be had by a man who is not standing in the room when the sleeve comes out of the cabinet. **The only thing that gets the leaf to Mosswake is Ivet Sarn's own rider, sent on the evening of the tenth on the district court's custody slip, with the applicant's name at the head of it.** The leaf comes back on the eleventh and is held sealed in the Mosswake strong box from that afternoon, and is produced in open court at ten on the twelfth, out of a Table sleeve with the Table's seal on the wax, on the magistrate's own direction and not on anybody's request, and is entered in the minute book as received into the custody of this court, with the rider's receipt and the date it left the building entered beside it.
- **The provincial hold** on the Venn file is sealed and its reference carries no office name. The old fire-and-water device of the First Seat is on the seal. It is named for the first time on the page by Tamsin to Marek on the channel bank at night on the tenth, in a private conversation, and for the first time **in open court** by Magistrate Rell in Chapter 7. No character may call it a First Seat instruction before Chapter 6, and no character may name it aloud in a room before Chapter 7.
- **Where the summary and the slip are.** The Venn summary was kept out of the courier's satchel on the evening of the seventh and is in Marek's inside coat; it would go north on the next courier if a supervisor ever signed the slip. The slip is in the same coat and is **unsigned** — Pell Vey refused to countersign it on an evening docket, and he retracts that promise himself in open court on the twelfth. The comparison request is a different sheet: Marek left the original on the Table's tray on the ninth, and it is still there at the end of the batch, unsigned. Do not put any of these three on a tray and in a coat at the same time.
- **How to read an hour.** The chapters use ordinal hours ("the seventh hour", "the second hour") and the sense shifts with the scene, so a later batch must not assume a single convention. What is fixed and matters: the courier leaves Auremar at dusk on the seventh; Sarn's rider leaves Mosswake at the seventh hour of the evening of the tenth and is at the Table at the second hour of the morning of the eleventh; the witness order goes up on the board at the eighth hour of the morning of the eleventh; the leaf is produced at ten on the twelfth; the ruling is made at twenty past three on the twelfth; and in Chapter 10, all on the eighteenth, in this order: the offer to have the three documents returned out of the inventory is made and refused at the eighth hour, the ledger is produced at the ninth hour of the morning and copied until the second hour of the afternoon, the chain opens at the fourth hour of the afternoon, the arrest is at the sixth hour of the afternoon, and the request is stamped into Examinations custody and the two of them come out at the ninth hour of the evening.
- **The exhibit sleeve** holds the source leaf, the witness copy, the filed correction, the Reed Cut memorandum, Pyle's certificate, and Tamsin's comparison copy, sealed and carried to the Mosswake registry and to no other office **except by a joint order of the Mosswake Roll Court and the Chancery district of Auremar made for the purpose of copying it**, which is how the sleeve lawfully reaches the room above the chandler's shop in Chapters 9 and 10. No copy of the six documents may be made except by the court or by a person the court names in open session; the twenty-six public copies are of the court's ruling and its five terms, which are not among the six.
- **The chain** also holds two sealed pages folded in behind the memorandum: the First Seat form, and a second sealed page whose contents have not been read. A thread of old red is caught in the fold. The chain was opened **twice**: once at the Mosswake courtroom on the night of the sixteenth, to receive and enter the joint order coming down from Auremar with a constable's name at the foot of it, which is the opening Chapter 9 sends the roll-keeper to, and once in Auremar at the fourth hour of the afternoon of the eighteenth, which is the opening that produces the form. **The joint order is also what puts a constable in the broker's office at all**: the room above the chandler in Candlewright Lane is where the copies are made and the record kept, and the office itself is worked in front of the constable for the two days. The exhibit is **not** opened before the fourth hour of the afternoon of the eighteenth, so nothing out of the sealed file has been produced at any earlier hour. The second page's contents are a live open thread and must not be resolved in Batch 0002.
- **The ledger** is ninety-one leaves, copied in full in the room above the chandler's shop in Candlewright Lane, with a public inventory and named witnesses from the bench outside. Corvin Dray is in the Auremar district house on a joint order.
- **The audit request** is a hand-signed nine-paragraph document dated the eighteenth, stamped *Received*, custody *Examinations*, with a file number written in ink on Tamsin's copy by the intake clerk and initialled. It is not before the Table, not before the Inheritance Desk, and its scope is undecided. **On the nineteenth of the tenth it was narrowed by the applicant's own signature** to the sale of copied witness marks and the supply of pressed matrices within the district of Auremar, the entries at Glasswater and Emberwatch being **reserved and not abandoned**, with a clerk's time written beside the signature by Tamsin. **On the eighth of the eleventh a two-page supplementary request was filed**, naming MC/FS, the base issue, the amendment sheet, both runs, the distribution line, and the signer, and it took a second number and a second *Custody: Examinations* stamp without the applicant having to ask. Examinations has granted thirty days, wants the two provincial exhibits back, has recorded the refusal to produce the second sealed page against the applicant, and has left Bryn Mawer's supplementary line in the file at the applicant's request.
- **The two provincial exhibits.** A Glasswater river-court file (a delta landing and cut, a three-year holder who is not related to anybody in the file, a sixteen-year-old in the surety line, a filing of the tenth month itemised as entry ninety-one) and an Emberwatch copy of an endorsement on a **dyers' house** instrument, itemised, with the word *Itemised* underlined beneath the number by a clerk writing for the next reviewer. They were admitted as exhibits in the Venn matter at Mosswake on the **fourth of the eleventh** on the clerk's own authority, over an application signed by Marek Kest on the third, and the copies went out to the parties the same day. Four copies were in four buildings by the fifth. The magistrate has been informed in writing and has not ruled.
- **The Reading of the ledger after Chapter 17.** The broker's business also includes **scale matrices**: the plates, not the seals, bought by people who have already decided what impression they want. Dray's statement of the **nineteenth of the tenth** is eleven pages with no person's name in it and one description of a place: a counting house on a row by the Kiln sheds, entered in the ledger as a mark — a filled square with a bar through it and a notch cut out of the top left corner — against **thirty-eight** lines in the *carry* column with the word *paid* beside it, in **three** districts (Auremar on the great majority, Glasswater on four, Emberwatch on two, one of each of the last two being the provincial entries named in the third paragraph). No street, no name, no initial. Dray has never been up the stairs.
- **The twenty-six public copies** of the ruling are in twenty-six households, not in one place, and the arithmetic is fixed and checkable: **nine** made by Tamsin, **six** by a professional copyist in Greyfen who charged nothing, **four** by the hooded woman from the seed barn, **three** by Ivo Harker out of his mother's tin, and **four** by two of the men off the Reed Cut bank who would not give their names and who made theirs together on the back of a seed tally, arguing about the fourth term. Twenty of the twenty-six were therefore made in the lane and six came in from Greyfen.

## Named Figures Added In Batch 0001

Recorded so later batches do not invent replacements. These are supporting figures with their own wants, not clues. Marl Crenn, Rennie Sallow, and Perry Ostrow are bound in Batch 0002 and are recorded in `bible/characters.md`; they are listed there rather than duplicated here.

- **Garren Pyle:** the certifier who attended the Mosswake hearing for Corvin Dray with the pressed certificate. Withdrew the record rather than read it, would not say whose hand pressed the matrix, and was held for name and instructing office.
- **Ivo Harker:** an old lane-man in the Venn lane who keeps his mother's bundle of lane copies in a tin under his bed and copies by hand. He made three of the twenty-six public copies on leaves out of that bundle, because he has not bought paper in four years, and the red-thread page is the leaf at the bottom of the bundle that he had never once wanted anything off, so the stitch sits in the margin of a page that also carries a court term two days old. He is the keeper of an uncatalogued local copy, not an agent of anything.
- **Brammel:** a client waiting on Corvin's bench, aged about sixty, who identified the green box under the window as the working box and not the archive box. One of eleven protected witnesses.
- **The unnamed man who gave his name as a firm:** the Chapter 10 offer. About fifty, well dressed, gives a firm instead of a person, and offers to have three documents of the sealed exhibit released out of the file before it is ever opened, free and unsigned, on the understanding that the copyist's record of them is altered, and says that a fourth document can be taken from the woman holding it in a lane in Reed Cut. Declined by Marek and by Dunnet together and minuted at the eighth hour of the second day. Nobody knows who sent him, he gives no name, and the attempt to reach the woman named in the twelfth is reported to the Mosswake court and is **unanswered on the page**. He is not an agent of anything on the page and must not be written as one.
- **The unnamed hooded woman of the seed barns:** makes copies in a schoolroom hand, will not give her name, and stayed until she had heard the ruling twice. Tamsin sent her a copy because a person who will not give her name is a person who intends to be hit.
- **The customs clerk on the Auremar quay:** not named, not a plot element. He told Marek a decision had reached a person he has never met, and at the end he says he is not asking for anything. He is the shape of the slow part of the work.

## Figures Named In Batch 0002

Full entries in `bible/characters.md` for the first four; the rest are recorded here so that a later batch does not invent replacements.

- **Marl Crenn,** fifty-one, the Greyfen dyers' schedule assessor, eleven years in the room, four exemptions signed. Holds the craft exemption form and its second box; frightened of a form rather than cruel. Chapter 15. Signed the exemption for this house, this year, on the foot of the amendment, and said out loud that she was not signing because she believed it.
- **Rennie Sallow,** the Mosswake upper-district household whose seed allocation was delayed when Sarn's file was open in the fifth year. Named and paid eleven pounds in Chapter 14. His daughter **Wenna Sallow**, nineteen, is on the reading-table rota.
- **Perry Ostrow,** thirty-five, a copyist in the copying room of a Glasswater river court, who entered the endorsement into the filing book on the third of the tenth month, told nobody at home, posted the sheets to the Mosswake lane on the twenty-ninth, and came up the river herself on the first of the eleventh. Her husband is blind since the spring, when he read the file summary at the top of the delta landing. Named in Chapter 19 and on the page in Chapter 16 as the bundle-coat woman at the Mosswake stair and at Sarn's window.
- **Bryn Mawer,** seventeen, Corvin Dray's copying girl **at a stone house two streets off the Kiln road**, not among the thirteen protected people and not on the bench. Named in Chapter 17, in a supplementary request of the eighteenth of the tenth. Wants to be examined in the copying and is not recorded as frightened, at her own request. **Three places in Auremar must not be conflated, because all three are named in the last four chapters.** Her *work* is the copying room in the stone house two streets off the **Kiln road**; her *lodgings* are a rented room in **Candlewright Lane** off a woman who has since taken a man from the chandler's trade into her front; and **Dray's office**, where the ninety-one leaves were copied and the public inventory was made, is the room above the **chandler's shop in Candlewright Lane** — which is not her workplace. The **row of counting houses by the Kiln sheds**, where the plates are bought, is a fourth place again. **Corrected at the Volume 01 close:** this line used to say the row was in no chapter a building anybody in the cast works in, and Chapter 48 makes that false — Bryn Mawer has been copying in the counting house for about five weeks, and the Cinder Court's record has been sitting on its counter since the sixth of the seventh. It is a workplace from Chapter 48 onward and was not one before it.
- **Ilsabet Roon,** about fifty-five, writes wills, marriage settlements, and small sea protests for the dock labourers, and cannot work because a man in a good coat told her clients to find another writer. One of the three protected people the order cannot help. Chapter 17.
- **Brammel:** now about sixty, eleven years a client of Dray's and forty years in the province, four papers in the green box with his name and mark, inventory item nine reworded at his request, and the box returned in a leather case with a receipt. He has his papers and does not have his name out of the inventory. Chapter 17.
- **The chandler of Candlewright Lane,** unnamed, whose stair has had a bar on it and a queue that has gone. Asked only that his trade loss be written down. Chapter 17.
- **Nevin Trost,** thirty-two, an examiner of Examinations with six years in the job. Granted a thirty-day extension in writing, tried to keep Bryn Mawer's line in the file, was made to record the sealed page's refusal, and handed over an unsigned offer he is not the man to make. Chapter 20. Not a villain and probably not a friend.
- **Nery Caudle,** thirty-nine, last house on the Greyfen lane, husband Mike keeps the bench and has for nineteen years, four children, one wage. Signed the amended guild clause on the twenty-ninth of the tenth with two pounds and five a quarter of her own wage in it. Chapter 18.
- **Coll Fenner,** twenty-eight, off the Reed Cut bank, one of the two men who made four of the twenty-six copies on a seed tally while arguing about the fourth term, now on the reading-table rota. Chapter 18.
- **The child of seven,** unnamed, sent by Bettany Skail to ask that a paper be read out loud before anybody signs, and deliberately left off the record by name. Chapter 18. Bettany Skail is the Orra Dunn neighbour of Chapter 13 who brought four pounds of tilling seed she could not refuse.
- **A Glasswater miller, a three-year holder who is not related to anybody in the file, a sixteen-year-old in the surety line, and an Emberwatch clerk who underlined the word *Itemised*.** All unnamed and all load-bearing. Chapter 19.
- **The Mosswake public register of pending duties,** begun in Chapter 13, kept at the clerk's window in Sarn's hand with a date, a household, a duty, and the next review. A district practice, not a new institution, and not a Roll Assembly.
- **The reading-table rota,** begun in Chapter 18: Ivo Harker, the seed-barn copyist entered as a role and left unnamed on purpose, Coll Fenner, Wenna Sallow. A levy sheet, four nails, and a piece of chalk. No clerk, no number, no court. **Superseded in Chapter 24.** The levy sheet is off the table leg and there is a chalk board on the frame of the trestle with the four questions on it, and the list of names on it is not a rota: anybody may add their own name and nobody may take another person's off. Wenna Sallow took her own name off it in the first month and put it back.

**Repair pass applied to Volume 09 Batch 0002 after its writer run** (`logs/batch-0002.review.log`). It changed no plot, invented no fact, and no chapter was restarted. What it moved, and the one finding it did not apply: **the reading's top finding called the dated week in Chapter 0419 "a date the calendar forbids" and "the only occurrence of 'twelfth month' in any chapter file in the repo", and the second clause is false — the reading's own sweep was `grep -rn "twelfth month" outline/ chapters/ state/ | head -20`, the `head -20` returned six `outline/` lines and cut the sweep off before it reached a chapter, and run whole the same sweep returns 109 files, one of them `chapters/volume-08/chapter-0396.md`, which is the chapter where the disclosure was made and whose date line matches 0419's day, week and month exactly. The month was canon and was left alone; applying the reading's remedy would have replaced a correct reference to a closed chapter with the date of an unrelated one.** What the reading's verdict did point at, without naming it, was a real error in the same sentence: the **year name** in 0419 stood a year after 0396's and now stands in 0396's year, and the wrong name is the one carrying four *after the* and the right one the one carrying three. And the **elapsed figure**, which no finding named, was wrong everywhere it was a present-tense claim: 0396 is the fourth week of the twelfth month and 0419 the first week of the seventh, which is twenty-five weeks and about six months, so four present-tense claims in 0419 are now six and one in 0415 is now five, **while the four months inside 0419's quotation of 0396 and 0415's report of the guess both stay four, because 0396 is closed and says four.** Also moved: **Marn Ottery's tenure in 0413 is eleven years and not nineteen**, the nineteen being the courier's and given in another mouth; **0411's two seconds and a second are one act and are now four minutes and a half in both places**; **0411's minutes now change hands on the page**, which they did not, and the older woman's own tenure is eighteen years where the line said nineteen; **0413's "that man is a carrier" is "the man from the yard is a carrier"**; **0414's man carries the age and the fair hand the state layer has been calling his since 0369, and the woman at the foot of the four steps is settled as his wife and not the day-book woman on the authority of closed Chapter 0369, which says so in terms**; **the woman of 0411 is about fifty-three and not about fifty-five, the man with the chain is about fifty-five, and the collision between them is gone from the page and from all thirty-seven lines of the six live state files and the Batch 0003 prompt, and no file in `state/archive/` was touched.** Craft: eight clusters broken and not the register, with "and I am not going to" from fifty-three to thirty-nine and "I am not going to be thanked" from eight to four. The ten files stand at **15,378** and the manuscript at **1,121,580**, and 1,121,580 less 14,325 less 15,378 is 1,091,877 exactly, and the figures before the repair, 15,296 and 1,121,498, were correct and are named and deleted nowhere.

## Figures Named In Batch 0003

Full entries in `bible/characters.md`. These are the only new named figures in the batch, and the two support figures a card is allowed are listed with them.

- **Iselle Oster,** forty-one, a cooper's widow at Millbrook Reach three hundred miles down the water, doing her own trade since the seventh year. The shop is **Oster and Son** with the *and Son* painted over and not painted out. Her son **Dain Oster**, twenty-two, has been out of the trade for a year. She wrote to a trestle table in a lane in the second month because a woman on a landing told her there was one, and she lost the master's gauge on the fourth of the twelfth. She is neither a claimant nor a plaintiff; she is a person with a missing instrument and a daughter on a surety line, and she wants the gauge back and wants to know whether the paper is a debt.
- **Tace Oster,** sixteen, Iselle's daughter, in the surety line of the instrument, signed nothing, four days out of a school term, and gave the fourth question twice with two different answers. She asked in the second week of the first month whether it was her fault and has not been asked that question since.
- **Sabra Ollett,** forty-one, clerk of the Millbrook Reach landing office, nine years in it. She stamped a creditor's filled-in model endorsement into the routine column in the tenth month in about four seconds, on a Thursday, because that is what a landing office does with what is put in front of it, and she cannot produce a number for the filing and has thought about those four seconds every day since the ninth of January. She is the **obedient clerk**: the person who proves that following a form perfectly is not the same as being safe. Not a conspirator, not a fool, and she told Tamsin Rook the truth about the stamp before she let her in.
- **Wendt Sayer,** the Reed Cut district works foreman, named in Chapter 11 and used again in Chapter 21 to price a hearing. Nine men, a boy, and a wet rope. He is the reason the cost ceiling is a real figure and he is the only person in the batch who refuses to make a bad number into a good one. He is a foreman and a witness by trade and is not a plot element.
- **The professional copyist on the Greyfen road,** unnamed and left unnamed, who made six of the twenty-six public copies for nothing in the ninth month and charged four pence a sheet in the twelfth, and said the free six were anger and that her shop has a window that says *copying* on it and she would like people to know there is a price. Eleven years in the same shop. Not a replacement for anyone.
- **The assessor from the next province,** unnamed, of a Weavers' and Small Dyemasters' Association with eleven houses, who came sixty miles in a cart with the Beckery's copy in a leather case in Chapter 27, was in the room when the fifth line on the back of the exemption form was read aloud, worked out in about eleven seconds what it did to a house with a boy on a term, and wrote the fourth question out at the top of a letter to eleven houses **without saying where it came from**. A decision in her own association's favour follows in Batch 0004 and is not granted in this batch.
- **The woman of about sixty-five at the seed barns,** unnamed, who produced the fourth question. Bettany Skail, Orra Dunn's neighbour of forty-one years' standing, is a different person and is at the top of the upper lane.


## Figures Named In Batch 0004

Full entries in `bible/characters.md`. These are the only new named figures in the batch, and the Emberwatch clerk remains unnamed by design.

- **Bettin Rahl**, the standing assessor of the **Emberwatch Dyers' Combination**, whose room is over the weigh-house office on **Sillrow** and whose hours are the second bell to the sixth. He answered one question in four lines and said plainly that the person was entitled to a plain answer, and told her the cost of the next step before she asked him twice. He is the only door a house in that trade is allowed to knock on, under a rule thirty-one years old at the second leaf of the Combination's book, and he wrote three lines across the top of the witness order that came back signed, of which the last is: *You asked what it will cost them. It will cost them one thing, which is that a person they have never met has written their name down in a book, and it cannot be taken out again, and I have told them that, and they have signed anyway, and I would like it noticed that I did not ask them to be brave.*
- **Osa Ferren**, of the fourth house past the weigh-house on Sillrow, in Emberwatch, one of the four who did not answer. She apologised for it in her first letter to the lane and wrote the first letter that trade has ever sent to a court, through its assessor, asking not what she should sign but *what a person does who is owed an answer.* She is a person, not a plot device, and she is owed a scene in a later batch.
- **The Emberwatch clerk who itemised entry ninety-one and underlined the word for the next reviewer** is a clerk of that same dyers' trade. The reason the filing is itemised is not that anybody broke the rule: **the rule was never read, because it was never issued to them.** It is still unnamed on the page and is not to be given a name in a later batch without a card.
- **The young clerk of the intake desk**, twenty-five or thereabouts, is a working figure and not a plot element. He has written the time in the margin in ink and initialled it **four** times for Marek Kest across Volume 01, three of them inside six months, has never once been thanked, was the witness to the refusal of the promotion, and wrote the fourth on the twelfth of the eighth at the counter when the Registrar reopened the Kest file. **In Volume 02's first batch he wrote two more and initialled both — one on a rider down to Mosswake at his own cost and one for a copyist — and has still never been thanked for either**, and he is one of the two persons who will examine Marek Kest in the Docket of Powers on the eleventh of the first month.


## Volume 1 Named Support Cast

- Ivet Sarn, thirty-eight, Mosswake Roll Court clerk. Cautious, not concealing; released the Venn source leaf under a recorded chain of custody and later testifies about the delay.
- Ostyn Vare, forty-five, foreman at the Greyfen dye-house where Nell works. Honest about wages, afraid of losing the craft exemption over the exit clause.
- Ruhl Dunnet, fifty-two, Auremar Chancery constable. Arrests only under a joint order and only after records are copied.
- Hallis Dren, thirty, clerk of the Reed Cut district water office. Signed the flood memorandum that the later correction was filed under; not a conspirator.
- Odile Fenn, thirty-four, Mosswake guild witness for canal work. Allies with Tavi's wish to be examined for work; wants apprentices able to leave a craft.
- Ages fixed for Volume 1: Mara Venn forty-three, Tavi Venn seventeen, Orra Dunn thirty-six, Nessa Dunn fifteen.
- Chapter placement, so no later batch invents a replacement: Sarn refused to reopen the file, recorded her refusal, and stated her four days in Chapter 3, produced the leaf in Chapter 7, and must name the household her four days cost in Chapters 11–18. Dren's flood memorandum set the Chapter 6 deadline and was produced and testified to in Chapters 7–8. Sivra Oris was at the channel in Chapter 2 and is named again in the Chapter 8 ruling; she testifies in Chapters 34–40. Vare carries the exit-clause challenge in Chapters 11–18. Dunnet made the Chapters 6–10 arrest, on the seventeenth and eighteenth. Fenn refused Tavi's examination in Chapter 9 and examines her in Chapters 41–50. Doctor Perrin Ashe of the Mosswake river landing is the man who told Marek that the reading had not let go of him, and to come to a person before a book; he may recur as an ordinary physician and owes nothing to the plot.
- **Ivet Sarn's four days are on the page and are not a later invention.** In Chapter 3, told to write down her reason, Sarn gives the great caution first: a file she reopened in the eighth month of the fifth year sat open until the fourth month of the sixth, and eleven hundred households ate four months late because the docket could not be closed and the relief rolls could not be certified. Then, separately, she adds one more thing and says it once: it took her four days to open it, she looked at it for four days looking for a way not to, and on the fourth day the relief rolls still could not go out. The four days are her own smaller sin inside the great one, and the household it cost is still unnamed on the page. Tamsin wrote *four days* on the board under the date. **What is still unspent, and what Chapters 11–18 owe the reader: which file it was, that it was an upper-district barn term file carrying the same substituted wording, and that the Rennie Sallow household's seed allocation was delayed. Sarn has a paper about that winter in a drawer in her own room and has never told them why.** Do not invent a new duration, a new year, or a new household. Use the fifth year and Rennie Sallow.
- Surname collision to hold: **Sivra Oris**, the Reed Cut water keeper and the scale counterparty to the Venn instrument, is not **Seryn Oris**, the off-page First Seat and the final antagonist. Both belong to House Oris, which is exactly why the names must never be merged on the page. Seryn is not named, present, or credited with any action anywhere in Volume 1, and the sealed First Seat instruction is her seat's paperwork rather than a personal order by her. Sivra speaks only inside her own competence, cannot answer for the First Seat, and is never made a mouth for a power she does not hold.


## Current Characters and Power

- Marek opened at Stage 0. He is still Stage 0 plus an unstable first Seam-Sight, earned on the page in Chapter 8. **He performs no magic anywhere in Chapters 11–30**, and **exactly one reading anywhere in Chapters 31–40**, taken in Chapter 40 under the undischarged limited Venn audit, which decides nothing and costs him ash, a headache, a nosebleed and two days of not being able to look at print. **He writes no valid exception, counter-seal, mixed warrant, true-name reading or Roll Assembly anywhere in Chapters 1–50**, and **the word "exception" appears nowhere in Chapters 31–40.** In Batch 0004 he refused a standing examiner of provincial filings with a room, a drawer and the standing to which forty-six districts would answer, in a room with a witness, with the terms entered and his signature under it, and he wrote the whole of the instruction that standing would have let him issue in his own book and filed it nowhere. In Batch 0003 the finding is that a *review date with no named person is not a review*, which is why the thing he accepts in place of a certified rule is a procedure with a named clerk, a witness, a cost ceiling and a fixed date — none of which is his power and none of which places any burden on his body. The cost of the one reading has been paid in full: the headache went on the twenty-sixth of the tenth month, and the temporary inability to lie about one named obligation **lapsed on the page** in Chapter 18 at the fourth hour, in a lane, to Wenna Sallow, and is described as a lapse and not a cure. It was used against him at least three times before it lapsed — the woman with the soup pot at the gate rail on the twentieth, Hallow Parrow in the corridor on the twenty-third, and Tamsin in the alcove in the eleventh month of the ninth — and the last of those was used as a substitution rather than a silence. He does not revisit Perrin Ashe, and the reason given is that there is nothing to pay a penny for. He minds the loss of the shield more than the loss of the headache, and says so. That inability is on the page three times. The first is in Chapter 9, in the Venn yard: Mara asks whether anything left in the file can come back for them, he opens his mouth to give her the sentence that would let her sleep, and it does not come, and Tamsin answers in his place and writes the unanswered question in her own book. The second is on the Auremar quay on the seventeenth, where he opens his mouth to say it to a stranger and nothing comes. The third is on the quay on the eighteenth, where there are four things he would like to say and may say only the one he is permitted to, so the limitation is a substitution rather than a silence. It is not a collapse and it is not free. No counter-seal and no Stage 2 ability appears in Volume 1.
- The first Seam-Sight is shallow. Marek can see one active chain and its immediate beneficiary. He cannot identify who first introduced it, and he has said so out loud rather than guessing. As established in Chapter 10, the red stitch and the thread in the form's fold are two facts of the same colour and are explicitly not joined in any sentence, in the record or in speech, until there is evidence.
- A reading can be accurate and still wrong: it reports the present legal effect of the record in front of the auditor, so an altered or incomplete record produces a correct answer about a false document. Volume 1 opened on exactly this gap and Chapter 8 closed it in the other direction, which is the point.
- The Chapter 8 panel reads: `Named: the present holder of the Venn field. Promised: the present holder may be joined as guarantor until full review. Carried after death: the record carries a guarantor duty to whoever occupies the field unless a new hearing ends it.` It does not name Tavi Venn, whose personal debt the same ruling voids. The reversal depends on that: the file now reaches whoever occupies the field, and the same sentence travels to the Dunn summary.
- The reading was entered in the Mosswake minute book and copied into the widow's hand by Sarn's direction, on Marek's request in open court. Tamsin holds a copy. It is a public record, not a private fact, and Marek insisted on that at the time.
- A reading reports the record, not the world. The case in Volume 1 is still carried by material comparison, witness order, ink, seal pressure, and custody.
- Court orders are not Marek's exception. Magistrate Rell and the Mosswake court issued their own interim, closed-door, and final orders in Volume 1, including the closed order preserving the Venn crop and releasing seed that she offered on the tenth and never issued, the five operative terms, and the public-necessity sentence; those place no burden on Marek's body and are never his reading. What does appear in the Roll-Answer is not a court order but the **filed record as it stands after** the court acts on it, and the public-necessity sentence is part of that record, which is exactly why the reading reports the guarantor promise the sentence supplies. That is the whole of the rule: a reading reports the operative record, and the court's own gloss is in the operative record. Marek writes no valid exception, counter-seal, or mixed warrant anywhere in Chapters 1–50. The word "exception" in Batch 0001 belongs only to the invalid draft in Chapter 5, which cannot be used: it was written by a clerk with no such power, it recites a comparison the clerk never made, and it names a party who was never heard.
- Tamsin is a roll-keeper whose ordinary copying, counting, and memory preserve evidence; she is not a magical auditor, has no power of any kind, and has independent professional judgment that has repeatedly overruled Marek's. In Batch 0004 she **stopped waiting to be the person who is asked and became the person who asks**, filing four lines over her own signature as a roll-keeper, in her own name, naming the district of Glasswater rather than the standing office, entirely unprotected and expecting nothing. She also went up the water a second time out of her own wages, not to help, and said in the abstract that a person who has been the one to ask should also be able to ask a person of power, and then declined to make the assessor of a second association answer one more question.
- Nell is a dye-house worker who wants paid craft independence and refuses to be protected by concealment. Her exit clause is amended, named, and accepted in Chapter 15, and the amendment is a numbered form that four houses on her lane have signed or will sign under fear. **In Chapter 24 she gave the reading table to the lane for good** and it runs without her, which she has decided is not a slight, and in Chapter 29 she did not write to her brother, twice, and examined the reason and did not believe her own first account of it. **In Batch 0004 she published the levy arithmetic about her own neighbours in chalk, with an apology in chalk under it, at a request from the person the number was about; she asked the fourth question of a person with power and got one clear answer and built no case out of it; she brought the Caudles' second paper out from under the cloth, which has a man's name in a box on it; and she did not go to Wenna Sallow's gate and wrote down the decision and the reason.** She has not written to Marek at all in this batch and put a letter from a furnace town on a table forty miles from him. She has been told about Ilyra and has not forgiven the ninth month and has not left.
- Pell is a mentor-shaped institutional antagonist, not the final enemy. In the yard behind the Chancery on the fourth day of the tenth month he asked Tamsin how many of thirteen protected people had the form, was refused, said he did not know the form existed and would not have acted on it, and gave her her own worry about a print run. **In Batch 0004 he offered Marek a standing examiner of provincial filings on condition that the Venn correction be treated as a routine filing defect, and he said the condition out loud in advance because, he said, saying it out loud is cheaper than the other way.** Marek refused, the refusal was entered and signed, and Pell now has his name on a reply and two recorded refusals in this matter. He warned Marek that listing the Standing Office for notice would make the file a series file in two years, and was right. He has known since the sixth of the twelfth that Tamsin holds a dated record of the yard and has let her keep it, and calls that the single worst supervisory act of his career and says he would do it again. He still has not been given the ninety words. **Tamsin told Marek the substance of the yard on the thirteenth of the twelfth, in the alcove, in one sentence, having decided that the letter going out to Magistrate Rell was what made it safe to say, and then gave him the whole of it including the line she had written under it and had not acted on for two months.** Pell then signed the reply of the thirteenth under his own hand, gave Marek the finding that the Standing Office of Provincial Continuities has no person at the top of it and the exact wording to use for it, said that he has signed district standing instructions nine times without asking who the authority was, and asked for the unfiled ninety-word corridor conversation of the ninth of the eleventh. He has not been given it. Corvin is the first concrete criminal and a valuable witness, and he remains accountable for his own crimes.
- Tamsin is the only slow-burn romantic relationship; no romance begins in Volume 1. In Batch 0002 she moved from the colleague who discloses by agreement to the colleague who decides and reports, and to a reciprocal arrangement in which Marek signs what is made in his own name and she strikes out of it what will not do. **In Batch 0003 both of them fail that arrangement once more, in mirror image** — he conceals Pell's request for nine days, she has concealed the question she wrote under the yard note for two months — and both disclose without being asked, and the difference is that she disclosed first and he did not. **In Batch 0004 he fails it a third time and softer: he decides the refusal of the promotion, gets it written and witnessed, and tells her four hours later, and she does not stop copying and asks one question.** Her live objection to leaving the First Seat quarterly return out of the reply **is no longer in his coat pocket** — she took it back on the ninth of the fourth month and put it in her own book between two pages of the Millbrook account, and recorded her reason for not moving it, which is that filing anything about a dragon seat's paperwork in the fourth month would merge the two documents in the file. **The new rule is on the page:** either of them may put a choice in writing with a date on it, and the other must answer in a room, in words, with a date on it. She has said she will check it in a year.

## The eight facts Volume 09 Batch 0005 puts on the page, and the one the outline of record puts there that the page refused

**One. The box of about four hundred blanks came out from under the far end of the boards at the top of four flights, in nine minutes, on the fourth day of the third week of the twelfth month of the seventh named year, and it was not put back.** It is on its side against the wall behind the far end, out of sight of the door where it had been out of sight of a door for eleven years, and the dust that had been on the top of it is on the deal in the shape of the bottom of it. **It is not the supply.** Chapter 0410 has Marn Ottery say *The box is not the supply* in her own mouth and that stands, and the outline of record's clause *a box of about four hundred blanks is the only supply of a thing that is bought about four hundred a year* **is a claim the page refused and it is not written into any chapter of this batch**, and the wrong clause is named here beside the page and deleted nowhere. The supply is the case at the near end, and nobody on that floor has ever been told where the case is filled, and that is Chapter 0422 and it is unchanged.

**Two. The man of about twenty-six who is paid by the corner carried the box down four flights and about four miles in the second week of the first month of the eighth named year, and put it down on the floor of a room on a second floor against the wall that has nothing on it, and it was not opened.** The lid has not been off it in six years and was not off it there and does not need to be. **He is a carrier in the page's own definition and he is paid for a corner and not for a page, and the young man from the shipping floor is not in any chapter of this batch and the two of them are never in one room, and neither is described with the other's noun.** The four miles is not one of the three locked distances: the four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times, and the fourth miles in Chapter 0443 is a road and not one of those, and **the page does not say whether it is the same four miles that the coat in Nell Kest's pocket is held four miles off, and no chapter of this batch compares them, and the close of this volume must not compare them either.**

**Three. The seventh named year ended at Chapter 0442 and the eighth named year begins at Chapter 0443.** The decision was the phase's to take and it is taken here, once, in prose, and it is not predicted anywhere earlier. **The seventh named year holds forty-six weeks against the calendar's forty-eight and is two weeks short, being the fourth month at two weeks, being Chapters 0409 and 0410, and that is unchanged and is not repaired by this movement.** The eighth named year is written out in full at each of its eight occurrences in Chapters 0443 to 0450 and is abbreviated nowhere, and **its name appears in eight of Volume 09's fifty chapters and in none of the forty-two before them.** The eighth named year holds eight weeks at the end of this volume, being the first month at four weeks and the second month at four weeks, and no month in this movement came out short and no date in it shifted.

**Four. A piece of paper with nothing printed on it is standing on a table against the base of about four feet of bare wall in the room taken by the week, and nobody sent it and nobody is going to be thanked.** It arrived at the door of that room in the second week of the first month of the eighth named year, folded in one, put there by a man who could not say where he got it and did not knock and is not going to be findable. **What is written on no paper in this volume is printed nowhere: not the one that went down the second hand's stair in 0431, not the one the young man from the shipping floor is still carrying in a coat, not this one.** The paper is on a table and is not on a form, is not in a book with an office on the cover of it, and is not a record.

**Five. Tamsin Rook worked out in the third week of the second month of the eighth named year that a person with something behind her is not available, and she did not say it out loud to anybody.** The finding is on the page in the chapter and not in a mouth, **and it is the volume's finding about her and not an organisation, and she is not made an organiser, a clerk with a title, a person somebody has finally asked, or a person who has been given a post, and her undertaking is live, unretired and unexercised and its date is still not said out loud.** The decision about whether she takes her colleague's judgment on a thing like this is still unmade and was not made in this chapter.

**Six. A man of about sixty-one signed the same sheet twice in the fourth week of the twelfth month of the seventh named year, and nobody told him and nobody could have, and he found out nothing.** **This is a new thing about him and it is not a number, and it is the first thing he has had to carry that is not a number, and the count of about nine sheets a year that are not what the person above him wrote is unchanged and is still nine and he is still the only person alive who knows which and cannot write one down.** He is not one of the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph and never is, and the man of about fifty-five with the chain is not one of those four and never is, and neither of them was put in a bay with anybody in this movement. The nine miles is walked zero times.

**Seven. A man was at the open side of the shed at the seventh hour and did not come in, and one of the two of seventeen stood in front of the board by the door and was not given the chance to say no.** The lamp is not lit before the seventh hour on any day of any week and no fire has ever been lit in that shed, and **the second half of a sentence a foreman of fifty-one began in a doorway has still not arrived, and nobody asked her for it and nobody is going to.** The four hundred yards is not walked in either direction. The man of about fifty-five spoke once, unprompted, and it was not a fifth sentence and nobody thanked him for it.

**Eight. A man came up a lane to the counting room at the back of a dye end about a book and did not get one, and there is no list of the fifteen volumes that are out on loan anywhere in this empire, and the man from the front office refused to write a lot number and was right.** **Nobody asked anybody anything in that room: the sentence about the fifth of the second lot was said to the front office and not to her, and it is a statement about a book and not a question put to a person, and the count of things asked out loud did not move.** The wage of nineteen days of a crew's money is still in a coat about four miles off, the paper with the printed ruled space on the back of it in that pocket is still clean, the sixteenth volume still has her name in capitals at the head of it and is still unopened, and the four hundred and thirty miles is walked zero times and she is not going up this river this season.

**And the ninth, and it is the arrangement, and it is the thing the close of this volume needs: nobody was thanked, nobody was forgiven, nobody was sent for, and nothing was resolved. The two people in their boxes are in their boxes and the form that put them there is not asked to be void by anybody. The question on the shelf under the window with no pane in it is still a question, it carries no full stop, its author is not going to be asked a second thing about it by anybody, and it is not printed out in any chapter. The bill at Lowcross is not named in this batch and is unpaid and nobody is liable. The drawer under the wall board is shut and two of the four things in it have never been opened, and the fourth item on that board is still the one none of the three clerks can account for. The count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven, and it is seven before this movement and seven after it, and the number is printed in no chapter of it.**

## What the repair changed, and the standing that a Volume 10 writer inherits from it

**One, the volume's plot state is unchanged and is stated here so that a reader of the section above and a reader of this one do not have to guess at the difference.** The box came out from under the far end of the boards in nine minutes in the fourth week of the twelfth month of the seventh named year and was not put back; it was carried down four flights and about four miles in the second week of the first month of the eighth year and set down on the floor of a room on a second floor and not opened. The man of about sixty-one signed the same sheet twice and found out nothing. A piece of paper with nothing printed on it is standing on a table against the base of about four feet of bare wall in a room taken by the week. Tamsin Rook worked out that a person with something behind her is not available and said it to nobody. A man was at the open side of the shed and did not come in and one of the two of seventeen was not given the chance to say no. A man came up a lane for a book and did not get one. **Nobody was thanked, nobody was forgiven, nobody was sent for, nothing was resolved, and the last line of the volume is unchanged and is the one the close prompt quotes.** None of the nine facts in the section above is altered by a single word.

**Two, the re-prints that were removed, and the closed chapters that were the far side of each one, because a Volume 10 writer must not walk into a re-print of any of them.** Against 0431: the man of about sixty-one's pen going back into the pot, and the young man from the shipping floor's opening. Against 0432: the man of about sixty-one not seeing him go. Against 0434: the man of about thirty-four with the fair hand's five nouns, his arrival at the door, his coat and its folded leaf, and the sentence about the gap at the foot of a sheet, **which survives at 0448 in new words and which is therefore a fact of the page and not a line of it, and the fact is still that a woman told him in the ordinary voice that the gap at the foot of a sheet is the exact width of a name.** Against 0437: the man of about fifty-five's reading of a paragraph, the shed's board and chain and lamp, the two sentences at the fourth hour, and the four sentences in the second week of the fifth month. Against 0438: the counting room's opening, its window, its board and its shelves, and the sixteen volumes. Against 0439: the woman at the bottom of four steps and her door, and the twenty minutes. Against 0401, 0403, 0410, 0416, 0418, 0420, 0422, 0424, 0426, 0429, 0430, 0433, 0435, 0440 and 0355: fifteen further clauses, each named one by one in the table in `state/batch-summary.md`. **No chapter before 0441 was opened for edit by this repair, and the four hundred closed files are unchanged at 1,091,877 words to the word.**

**Three, the formula list, which is a thing a writer measures and does not inherit, and which now stands at twenty enumerated entries.** The refrain *the count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is the same as it was on the…*, in 0407, 0410, 0420, 0440, 0449 and 0450 and in no other chapter of the fifty; the triadic *nobody thanked anybody / was forgiven / was sent for*; **the empire-formula and its three clause-boundary variants**; *the exact width of a name*; the counter's closing ritual and the four-items clause; *the space at the foot of a sheet is the exact width of a name*; *is a thing two people have to agree about*; *four hundred yards up that lane was not walked*; *there is no fire in that room*; *who keeps minutes in a room off the old river road*; and the four character-identifying clauses. **And the standing, which is the fourth time in this project that a false zero has expired and the first time the cause has been a list: a classifier whose formula list is too short does not report prose for the formulas it is missing, it reports zero, and a zero with a working positive control is the most convincing result these instruments can produce and the least informative — and a control must therefore be drawn from outside the list, because a list's own contents are something the instrument knows by construction and a control planted on one of them tests the mechanism and not the coverage.**

# THE VOLUME 07 THREADS AT THE OUTLINE, AND THE ONE THAT IS THE HANDOFF, AND IT IS A SHAPE AND NOT AN INSTRUMENT

*Appended by the run that took `workspace/volume-07/volume-07-outline/PROMPT.md`, the volume-outline phase, which writes no prose. Nothing above this line is rewritten, edited, deleted or moved, and no row above this line is closed by this section. Every row below is in the present tense, every row carries a Volume 07 or later payoff target or an explicit em dash, and the first row is the handoff itself. The full state of the handoff's components is in the closing section of this file above and is not restated here; this section adds the threads the outline opens and does not repeat what is already recorded.*

**THE VOLUME 07 HANDOFF, AND IT IS THE ONE ROW THAT MATTERS MOST IN THIS FILE, AND IT IS THE SAME ROW THE VOLUME 06 CLOSE OPENED AND IT IS NOT CLOSED BY IT.**

| **How a thing is asked in about nine hundred buildings at once by people who cannot be instructed to ask it — the shape question, and it is a shape and not an instrument** | **OPEN, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING VOLUME 07 INHERITS, AND IT IS NOT THE WHO.** A practice is in two people about four hundred and thirty miles apart with no list of them and no form and no heading and no fund, and **nobody in either building knows that the other one exists.** About nine hundred entries a year still come in under a heading, a second hand is at the foot of every one of them, and that second hand has never been asked anything in about nineteen years. A single return goes to one district out of about nine hundred districts. **Nobody has yet worked out how a thing is asked in about nine hundred buildings at once by people who cannot be instructed to ask it, and the outline's answer is that it cannot be, and the answer is a finding and not a method, and no instrument in this empire would answer it and none is wanted.** The who is Volume 06's and goes on unanswered, and unanswered is not the same as closed | **The Volume 07 outline, which has now declared the answer, and then Volume 07's own shape, and not this file** | **It is not closable by a volume that answers the who instead, and a Volume 07 that reaches for a post, a commission, a warrant, a circular, a return or a fund is reaching for the instrument the question is not about** |

He said all of it out loud at a rail on the second day of the second week of the second month of the year after the year after next and it went into a room and not into a book, and nobody thanked him | **Volume 07, and the volume's climax is a man who comes nine miles for the third time and does not ask him anything, and the reason is given out loud in about nine sentences** | **Not closable by a document, and a document with a disagreement in it is a form, and a form is a heading, and a heading is a company** |

| **The difference between saying and asking, which is this volume's rule and is not on the page in this form** | **OPEN, AND THE OUTLINE ESTABLISHES IT IN ITS FIRST MOVEMENT.** A person may say a thing out loud in a room and may not ask a thing out loud at all, because being asked is being served and being served is a party and a party is the only person who can be told what a thing is going to be used for, which is the second of Volume 06's three rules carried forward and not re-derived. **A saying costs the person who says it nothing that any paper can hold, and an asking costs the person asked everything, and it cannot be undone, and a room in which a question is put becomes a room in which a record exists** | **Volume 07, all five movements, and it is the rule the volume turns on** | **Not closable by a form, because a form is the machine that asks, and the machine is what the rule is about** |
| **The address cannot be asked in the building that made it, which is the volume's reversal** | **OPEN, AND THE OUTLINE DECLARES IT AT Chapters 0324 to 0327.** A question put in that room is a question put into a record, and the record is what the sheet goes in, and the last time a thing of that shape happened to about four hundred people their sheet went back. **The arrangement that has kept about nine hundred sheets a year correct for nineteen years is the arrangement that has kept anybody from asking the second hand one question, and those are the same fact and not two facts** | **Volume 07's third movement, and the cost of finding it out is that the whole of it has now been said out loud twice by the same man, and a man who has said a thing twice is findable by the saying of it, and about nine people were in that room** | **Not closable by moving the asking, because the asking has nine miles and about four hundred and thirty miles outside that room and there is no form for sending a man to ask a question** |

## Threads this batch moved, and by how much

1. **The fourth rule is now on the page twice, in two mouths, about four hundred and thirty miles apart.** Chapter 0331, a man of about thirty-four, in an empty lane off the Slade, in three turns. Chapter 0337, a woman of twenty, to one woman in a counting room, in about four minutes. **The two people do not know each other exist, neither has been told the other said it, and nothing in this empire would let either be told.** Chapter 0340 says that joining them nowhere is the last shape the finding takes in this volume. Both were said about four minutes, both cost something, and neither was thanked.

2. **The woman of twenty's rule moved from her head into the world, and it did not reach anybody it was aimed at.** In Chapter 0329 she had it and nobody to tell it to. In Chapter 0335 she has been carrying it round two doorways for about three weeks and has not said it. In Chapter 0337 she says it to one woman of the four, and the woman is told she is not being told that she is not paid, and **the two women she cannot reach are still two women she cannot reach and she had known they would be before she said it.** One of four women has now been told a rule and one of four has been told a wage, and those are not the same woman, and the two of them who have been told nothing have been told nothing.

3. **The foreman of fifty-one and the man with the fair hand are closer and no further.** Chapter 0332 is the day he does not ask, from her side, and Chapter 0333 is his side: he has worked out that a man who is owed a sentence cannot ask for it without becoming a document. **He now knows that asking would make him a document about one woman, and he is not going to write it down, and the second sentence is still owed and still not asked for and the day he asks is still the day she stops.**

4. **The clerk of about fifty-three has said the third absence and has said it once.** Chapter 0336: the not asking, the not writing, the not telling, and they are one arrangement. **She has stated in her own mouth that it is the last time in this volume any of the three gets said out loud in a room, and the three are now standing on their own without her.** She is not told that the man of about thirty-four is not coming back and there is no form that would let anybody tell her.

5. **The man of thirty-four is now within a hundred yards of a bay and has not gone in, once, and nobody asked him why.** Chapter 0331. He is owed and is not owed: a bill that is not named in these ten files, a form for asking a person whether they will mind being told something that does not exist, the thing nobody thanked him for, and a wife at the foot of four steps who is not thanked either.

## Threads this batch did not touch, and the state of each

6. **The address, a man of sixty-one, has not been in any of these ten chapters and walked zero times.** He has had his third visit and said the whole of it twice, in Chapter 0323 and once before it. He is nine miles off, the season is over or going, and about nine hundred sheets a year are going to go on going out of that room with a hand at the foot of every one of them. **He is not told that a man of about thirty-four has been within a hundred yards of a bay and has not gone in, and there is no form in this empire that would let anybody tell him.**

7. **The woman of about twenty-six at the lock of the cold passage was not in these ten chapters and did not hand on her figure.** Chapter 0340 says the figure is in her head, has gone up, is not going to be handed on and is not going to get a heading, that she is not coming up a stair in this season, and that nobody is going to ask her what she counts. **The passage and the rail and the four hundred yards of cold flags are referred to in Chapters 0331, 0336, 0337 and 0340 as a room the fifth movement is going to use, and nothing has been spent.** **This entry said she was at the end of that passage, which is false against the page and is named here and deleted nowhere: she is at the lock, and the room with the rail is at the other end of the same four hundred yards and is not hers, which is Chapter 0358's title and 0393's third line, and the room at that far end is entered twice a week by the woman of about forty with a scuttle and is where Chapter 0362 happens. The false placement put her in the other woman's room, which is a merge this project has spent a volume preventing, and no Volume 09 row may carry it forward.**

8. **The undertaking of the fourth of the first month is live, unretired, unamended and unexercised, and no new ordinal was given to it in Chapter 0339.** The reason is the same one it has been and it is a fact about her and not about him: a person who is not asked has not been given a duty, and she has known that since about the seventh month of next year. **He is not at a stair, nobody sent him, nothing in this empire would let anybody send him, and there is no form in this empire for telling the person a thing did not happen to either.** She is at a counter four miles off and is not going to be told. The decision about whether she trusts his judgment is unmade and is not on the page.

9. **The four men in a bay who cannot read a paragraph were not asked one question about a number in any of the ten chapters.** The man of about fifty-five with a chain is in Chapters 0332 and 0338 and is not one of the four and says so. **The four are not a route, they are not a method, and Chapter 0337 says that out loud in a mouth.** The mark in chalk is a mark in all three bay chapters and is not converted in any of them.

10. **The two of seventeen: present in Chapters 0331, 0332 and 0338 and unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for in all three, and not going to start.** No chapter of the three explains why and no chapter of the three narrates their silence as a cost they are bearing. **The reader's rate is on the page as a rate: forty-five pence a day and four days a week, and a reader's day anywhere between fourpence and a shilling according to what is put in front of her.** Four shillings a year is the Company's whole money and is the rent of a hired store and is in a different building four hundred yards up a lane, and the two figures are not compared in any chapter.

11. **The bill at Lowcross stands at nineteen pounds three and fourpence, unpaid, nobody liable, and it is named in none of this batch's ten chapters.** The chapter written in the room that man works in did not name it, and the chapter that hands the fifth movement its room did not name it, and he did not pay it and is not the reason it is unpaid.

12. **The clause in the second of the eleven books is still a clause, carries no period, and its author is not going to be asked a second time.** **No chapter of this batch states an elapsed period from it, and the reason is inherited and is not a decision of this batch**: closed Chapter 0295's figure of about fifty-eight weeks cannot be reconciled with the two closed chapters that date the same question. The prohibition on stating a period was lifted by the review repair of Batch 0002 and the permission is real; **Batch 0004 did not use it and a later phase with a reason to use it may.**

## Two items this batch adds, both facts about measurement and not about the page

13. **The fifteen-word window's count moves by a factor of two and a half between two honest readings of one text, and a standing check list that prints one of them without naming the unit is reporting a figure about a different question from the one it names.** Measured as distinct runs keyed by their own text over a whole-file slide: Batch 0003 against Chapters 001 to 320 returns 147 and the recorded figure is 141, and this batch against Chapters 001 to 330 returns 122. Measured as per-reference-file instances on the same files and the same reference set: 324 and 362. **The blind spot written beside it: a count of instances answers how many times a passage was matched and a count of distinct runs answers how many passages there are, and only the second is a defect count.**

14. **The required year-name date line is between fifteen and twenty-two words and appears once in every chapter of this volume, so a fifteen-word sweep against the manuscript returns at least one run per chapter however the prose is written.** Sixteen of this batch's 122 distinct runs are that line and a hundred and six are narrative furniture; ten of Batch 0003's 147 are that line and a hundred and thirty-seven are furniture. **A batch handed a fifteen-word figure should separate the calendar line out before treating the number as a measure of its own prose, and should expect a floor of about one per chapter rather than a zero.**

The chapter is written at the house. ## What is still open at the close, in one place, and what a close may not do to it

**Still open and still not asked:** the who, which is Volume 06's, and unanswered, which is not the same as closed; the second half of the question, which is not asked in any of the three hundred and fifty files and is not restated in this section in any form a writer could put in a mouth; the next asking, which is nobody's yet. **Still standing and still unresolved:** both people in their boxes, the form that put them there not asked to be void by anybody, the question in the second of the eleven books still a question and carrying no period with its author not asked a second time, the figure at the end of the cold passage in a woman's head and gone up and not handed on and without a heading, the guarantee offered and unanswered with about sixty children inside it and unprinted in its own words, about nineteen people behind the bank, the Lowcross bill at nineteen pounds three and fourpence unpaid with nobody liable, about four men in a bay unasked about a number, a girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen unspoken to and unthanked and unsent for, and nobody thanked anywhere. **Still separate and still to be kept separate:** the two women about four hundred and thirty miles apart, neither of whom has ever heard of the other one, and the nine miles off a building off the old river road, which belongs to a man of about sixty-one and to neither of them, and the woman of about twenty-six at the lock of that passage, who is a third person and is nine miles off the lane off the Slade, **and whose place at the lock and not at the far end of those four hundred yards is corrected below and is the one the page gives in 0358's title and 0393.** **Still two things and never merged:** the two documents, four hundred and thirty miles apart, in two buildings, with no instrument joining them, and only Marek Kest and Tamsin Rook know both exist and neither of them says so. Still in no reply: the quarterly return, which does not appear in this volume either. Still dormant and armed and known to nobody in the story: the other return of the eleventh of the tenth. Still four ages and never a chain: the four appearances of the substituted wording, with no fifth added. Still three things: the three stitches, no two of them ever joined in a sentence. Still shut: the two sealed pages, with two refusals between them and no third, and the bundle, shut and unnamed, and the sealed witness house unvisited. Still a mark: the counting-house mark, unconverted. Still unentered: the year in the run. Still unprinted: forty-four thousand eight hundred and nineteen. Still a fact about the copying: a gap in a copy, with a body having directed that nobody be asked about the leaf it is on. Still five operative terms and never four: the Venn ruling, its schedule referred to zero times and the word not occurring in any chapter of this volume.

**And what this close may not do, and did not do: it may not name the who, may not restate the second half, may not resolve anything, may not thank anybody, may not merge any two of the three people this volume keeps apart, may not make a period out of a clause, may not give a heading to a figure, may not add a fifth appearance of the substituted wording, may not print the schedule or the word, may not pay or forgive or fund the Lowcross bill, may not put a period at the end of the question in the second of the eleven books, may not make the decision about whether a woman trusts a man's judgment, may not put a man at a stage, may not pay his reason for not reaching one a second time, may not reopen a single closed chapter, may not amend `outline/volume-07.md` or `outline/series.md` or `outline/ending.md`, and may not write a marker in its own directory.** **The measure of a good close is how little it changes and how exactly it states what is still standing. Nothing is resolved, nobody is thanked, and the lamp is not lit.**

OPEN — a formula list that is too short makes a classifier return a clean zero instead of prose, and a zero with a working positive control is the most convincing result this project's instruments can produce.** The twenty-word window over Chapters 0441 to 0450 was reported as 0 prose, 0 prose, 0 prose in three files at once, with a control that fired, and the true figures are 4, 18 and 0 and 3, 38 and 0. The list had eight entries and the volume needs twenty, and the nine it was missing include the empire-formula *there is no form anywhere in this empire in which a person is entered as the one who…* and four character-identifying clauses the batch prompt itself uses to keep two men apart. **Nothing is left to close here and the list is now enumerated in `state/batch-summary.md`; what is open is the standing, which is: when a list is the thing doing the classifying, the control has to be drawn from outside the list, or the control is a test of the list and not of the page. A list's own contents are something the instrument knows by construction, and a control planted on one of them confirms the mechanism and not the coverage. Every volume's formula list from here is measured by hand against the classifier before it is believed, and no phase may print a window figure it has not measured in the pass that prints it.**

**104. OPEN — a filter that never fires does not announce itself, does not throw, and returns a figure that looks exactly like a finding.** The section-break filter in this repair's own instrument was `if '--' in tokens` where `tokens` is a list: a list-membership test where a substring test was meant, silently always false, and it fired on nothing across two full runs while admitting two identical internal hits that were visibly a `---` followed by a sentence. It is fixed. **This is the seventh filter in this project's instruments found doing nothing and the first one found by a figure disagreeing with itself rather than by a reviewer looking for it, and none of the seven has ever produced an error message, which is the whole of why they are dangerous. No instrument in this project is to carry a filter whose failure mode is silence, and every filter is to be tested once by feeding it a case it must catch.**

**105. OPEN — a state record named a fix it had not made, inside a paragraph about stale word counts, while the defect it described was on the page.** The Batch 0005 record stated that Chapter 0449's closing ritual had been rewritten because it re-printed Chapter 0441's in the same words. Twenty-three identical words stood in the page when that sentence was written and stood in the page when the review found them, and they are out now. **A record that names a fix it did not make is worse than a record that never names the fix, because the second kind gets checked and the first kind gets trusted. No phase may write the word *rewritten*, *removed*, *corrected*, *is out* or *now reads* about a chapter, a figure or a formula without having re-run the check that would show it, in that phase, after that phase's last edit — and the batch that wrote that sentence had in fact run the check, and the check had returned zero, and the zero was wrong.**

# THE CLOSE OF VOLUME 09 — EVERY THREAD CARRIED FORWARD AT FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY CHAPTERS, NO THREAD CLOSED, NO STATE RESOLVED, NO DEBT DISCHARGED

*Appended downward by the phase that took `workspace/volume-09/volume-close/PROMPT.md`. The full close is in `state/archive/volume-09-close.md`. **No row above this point is rewritten and no thread is closed, because a close that closes a thread is a phase that resolved something, and this volume resolved nothing and this close resolved nothing.***

**OPEN — the arrangement. Nobody was thanked, nobody was forgiven, nobody was sent for, and nothing was resolved, and it is the ninth volume in which the count of thanks is zero.** OPEN — the two people in their boxes are in their boxes and the form that put them there is not asked to be void by anybody. OPEN — the question on the shelf under a window with no pane in it is still a question, it carries no full stop, it is not printed out in any chapter, and its author is not going to be asked a second time. OPEN — the girl of seventeen and the reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for, and not going to start. OPEN — the sixteen volumes are about four hundred and thirty miles up this river, fifteen are on loan, and there is no list of the fifteen anywhere in this empire. OPEN — the wage of nineteen days of a crew's money is in a coat about four miles off. OPEN — the bill at Lowcross was named once in this volume, in Chapter 0433, is unpaid, and nobody is liable for it. OPEN — the drawer under the wall board is shut and two of the four things in it have never been opened. OPEN — the fourth item on that board is in Marn Ottery's own hand, is about four years old, and none of the three of them can account for it. OPEN — the count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven, and this volume did not move it, and the number is printed in a record and in no chapter of any volume.

**OPEN, and new in this volume's last movement, and not resolved: a blank got to a man who could not be found and nobody sent him.** A box of about four hundred got to a room four miles from the counter that sells them, through four flights and in a carrier's two hands, and was not opened, and the carrier is now a man a courier saw on a road. A piece of paper with nothing printed on it went on a table in a room taken by the week, and then stood against about four feet of bare wall where he can see it, and the man who brought it came back once with nothing in his hands and said he was not going to come a third time, on the ground that gratitude has to be agreed at both ends of it. **OPEN — where the paper is now is not said, and the man who is paid by the corner has said out loud that he is not going to be findable and has not said where it is.** OPEN — a man of about twenty is about four hundred and thirty miles up this river and is not paid and is not going to ask what it is held against, and the four hundred and thirty miles is walked zero times. OPEN — a man of about sixty-one is still the second hand and has been handed a thing that requires nothing of him for the first time in about nineteen years, and he does not know what it is for and is not going to be told. OPEN — a foreman of fifty-one is still inside a box entered by a class and has given four sentences out loud and been asked nothing.

**OPEN, and this close adds four threads that are not plot and are the only findings in nine volumes still open in the same shape: one, a run of twenty words or more in a volume of fifty chapters cannot be seen by an instrument run inside a batch of ten, and Volume 09's twenty pairs were all across batch boundaries and the largest is ninety-nine words. Two, a formula list entry longer than the twenty-word window is invisible to the classifier, and the volume's largest formula is such an entry, and the figure it produces is the window's length and not the re-print's. Three, four elapsed figures in three places in Volume 09 do not support themselves against the volume's own date lines and are named in the close record and are not repaired. Four, a floor checked once a movement, by reading, passed five times and is met in two movements of five, and the check that would have seen it is a table across the whole volume and not a check inside one movement.** None of the four is a plot and none of them is a craft matter about a room.

**And the four debts, restated in full, and this close discharges none of them: an owed review of Volume 04's Batch 0005, four volumes on; owed second readings of Volume 05's Batches 0003, 0004 and 0005 and of Volume 06's own Batch 0003, which is four and not three; the review gate, which has fallen back to the writing agent on every phase the history records and has never once produced a review that could be certified independent, and a gate that only ever falls back is not a gate that passed either; and the open items that are not plot, with the sentence bound among them, which are eighty-nine by the high-water mark and not a count of anything, and the sixty-three this project has been quoting is twenty-four short of the eighty-seven measured before the eighth enforcement and twenty-six short of the high-water mark, which is item 90, and it is not corrected in place in the records that state it as a count. **This clause was amended in place by the repair of the Volume 09 close, which found the twenty-four sitting beside the eighty-nine without saying which of the two it was short of; item 90 above is the ledger's own account of all three figures and is not disturbed, and the figure first printed stands in `state/archive/volume-09-close.md` and is deleted nowhere.**

*Written by the phase that took `workspace/volume-10/volume-10-handoff/PROMPT.md`. No thread below is closed and no status is changed. The count of things anybody has asked out loud is seven; the next asking is nobody's yet and this handoff does not make it anybody's.*

**106.
