# WHAT VOLUME 07 BATCH 0001 DID TO EACH PRINCIPAL, AT CHAPTER 310

*Appended by the run that took `workspace/volume-07/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`, the first batch of the open volume. **The consolidated one-entry-per-principal position at Chapter 300 is above this section and is not replaced by a second set and is not restated here: this section records only what the ten finished chapters changed, names the movement each change belongs to, and carries an owed debt, a refusal and an unanswered question in every entry, because a consolidation that loses one of them is worse than no consolidation.** Nothing here is resolved. Nobody is thanked. Nobody is sent. The four hundred and thirty miles is walked zero times and the nine miles is walked zero times. New named figures in these ten chapters: none, and that is twelve consecutive batches and it is the standard.*

**The man of about thirty-four with a fair hand — the count, and the finding, and two chapters eight weeks apart, which the review of Volume 07 Batch 0001 corrected from *ten*, because Chapter 0301 is the first of that batch's ten and Chapter 0309 is the ninth and the step from each to the next is exactly seven days.** **Chapter 0301 is his ordinary week, and he is on nobody's list, and the volume opens on a man who does not ask one question.** He goes through the rest of it about once in four weeks and this is the once, and the count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven and has not moved and he has not moved it, and the figure is printed once in the whole batch and it is in his room. **He wrote out one sum for a man who cannot pay him until the spring, the woman of about forty with a scuttle lit the lamp early, his wife did not ask him how the week went, and nobody thanked anybody.** **Chapter 0309 is the same man ten weeks on, and the discovery in it is structural and not a feeling: a question in this empire is asked of a person and not of a room; the only person in a room who can be asked is the one whose hand is at the foot of the thing; a hand is the most findable thing there is about a person; a name in a column is a thing a person can be served at; nobody is served anything to compare a hand against; so the address is about nine hundred rooms with one address in each and no way to find one of them from outside the room — and the only thing this empire has ever put in front of about nine hundred rooms at once is a class, a class is a heading, a heading is a company, and the whole of the machinery of asking at a scale is the machinery of making people into companies.** He said it out loud to about four feet of bare wall with a nail in it, and the wall did not answer, and the lamp was not lit, and he did not go and look at anything and nobody thanked him. **Owed and unpaid, and none of it paid by this batch:** the bill for being findable, which is not his and stands on somebody else's account; a form in this empire for asking a person whether they will mind being told something, which does not exist; the thing nobody thanked him for; and the eighth question, which is nobody's yet. **His refusal in this batch:** he did not go and look, twice, and he did not turn the finding into a speech. **His unanswered question:** how a thing is asked in about nine hundred buildings at once by people who cannot be instructed to ask it, and the half of it that is not the who, which nobody has asked and which this batch did not ask.

**Tamsin Rook, the clerk of twenty-four at the fourth counter — asked nothing, and what she worked out, and the decision that is not made.** **Chapter 0304 is her chapter and she is asked nothing in it, and that is entered as a choice and not as a fault.** A man came up that stair twelve weeks ago wanting nothing at all and asked her one question in the plainest words anybody has used in that room in two years, and she did not answer it, and the not answering took her about four seconds and she is not going to be told why. She has wanted to be asked every working day since about the seventh month of next year, and a person who is not asked has not been given a duty, and she has said the whole of it out loud to about four people and not one of them could do anything about it. **What changed in her in this chapter is a working-out and not a decision: the line she put in her own hand in the third month of last year, recording that a clerk of thirty-four said no on a stair and gave no reason, is a wall, and she has worked out that it is a window, because there is not one form anywhere in this empire that will take a line back out of a book a woman keeps for herself, and a line that cannot be taken back is the one kind of paper here that opens both ways — and the name at the top of that line is the name of a person who cannot be got at.** **Her undertaking of the fourth of the first month is live, unretired, unamended and unexercised, and the sixth reason is not a variation of the first five: nobody asked her, and this batch did not ask her either, and that is the whole of the new thing and it is not much and it is hers.** **The fourth of the four things in her drawer is untouched, unsent and unopened, with three others, and the two boxes drawn on the other page are not opened, not counted and not said.** **Owed and unpaid:** the answer to the question she was asked and did not give; **the decision about whether she trusts anybody's judgment, which is unmade, is not on the page, was not made in a room by this batch and is not made for her**; a fourth box, if there is one, which she will not say; the price of being a party, said out loud ten times and never once thanked; and about four hundred blanks' worth of nothing under the other end of that counter. **Her refusal in this batch:** she did not answer the question from twelve weeks ago, she did not rule a third line, she did not open the fourth thing, and she did not ask him whether he meant it. **No romance begins and none is implied, and a card or a chapter that reaches for one has left this manuscript.**

**Marek Kest, thirty-eight — a refusal and a non-use, both paid for, and nothing exercised.** **Chapter 0305 is the power chapter and it exercises nothing and attempts nothing.** He does not attempt the reading and gives the reason out loud in the room, to himself and to about four feet of wall: **two attempts have already taken two separate days of his mother's own history out of him, he is thirty-eight, he can no longer remember whether he left a room or stood in a doorway on the sixth day of the third month when he was eleven, and the third one is not a thing he is going to spend on a man at a rail.** He does not exercise the thing he is able to exercise, and a correct non-use is entered as one, and the reason is about nine words: there is no form in this empire for compelling a person to be brought to a room. He is not at a stage and is not going to get to one and the volume's one exercise of Stage 2 was paid in Chapter 0299 and is not paid again. **A bar of his own came off him on the twelfth of the ninth month of last year on an application of one line which he wrote himself, and that sentence is paid in these ten chapters in those words and is not varied.** **The mark on the inside of his left wrist is about three inches long and it is a symptom and not a power: it reads nothing, it decides nothing, it does not know where the ford is, and the wage is the price, and the price of what he did in the second week of the twelfth month of the year after the year after the year after next was a shilling and sixpence and that mark.** **Owed and unpaid:** nothing, in the sense that he is owed no money and no stage; the labour he chose out of his own hand in the fourth week of the eighth month of the year after the year after the year after next is not re-decided; nobody thanked him for a thing he did not do and there is not one form anywhere in this empire that requires a person to be thanked for not doing a thing; and there is nobody in this matter who could tell him to stop, which is why he is the most dangerous person in it and why nobody in it can protect him. **His refusal in this batch:** the third reading, and the thing he is able to exercise. **His unanswered question, which is the volume's own and is not his:** what a question put in a room where a person's own work is made costs that person, and nobody has asked it of him and he is not going to be asked.

**The man of about sixty-one who signs at the foot of every sheet — the address, and an ordinary day of it, and no question in it.** **Chapter 0307 is his chapter and it is not a confession.** He is sixty-one, he has been the second hand since he was forty-two, he signs about nine hundred sheets a year out of that room for people who cannot write and for people who are not in the room, and **he cannot read a paragraph.** He has read every one that he could read. **About nine of them in about nineteen years have not been what the person above him wrote, and he signed those nine because he was not asked and was given nothing to sign against**, and he has them in his head the way a man has a face in a crowd and could not put a year to more than two of them and could not write one of them down. **There is not one form in this empire that would let a man who cannot read a paragraph put his mark beside a sum and call it the mark of a man who disagrees, and he would want about four minutes to say no to about half of them and yes to the rest, and there is nobody to ask.** On every one of about nine hundred sheets a year there are three things that can be asked and two of them are a clerk and an office, and neither of those is a person anybody can put a question to, and that leaves him. He said all of it out loud once, about a year ago, standing at a rail, and it went into a room and not into a book, and a woman of about forty with a scuttle was in that room, and there is no form that would let anybody ask her what she heard. **Owed and unpaid:** about four minutes; about nine sheets; the reason nobody has asked, which is that he would tell the truth; and the two halves of the arrangement, which are the same arrangement and which he has never put in one sentence. **His refusal in this batch:** none is available to him and none is claimed; he asks nothing, he is asked nothing, and a carrier is paid ninepence at a lock and has not been asked what she is carrying in about six years and neither has he. **His unanswered question:** whether a man who signs about nine hundred things a year and is asked about nine of them can be a man who is sometimes right, and the answer to that is that a minute with an answer in it is an order and no form lets a clerk of that office enter one, and nobody has ever put that to him.**

**The clerk of about fifty-three in the office of a seat — the season, and a thing that is not going to be arranged.** **Chapter 0310 is her chapter and the movement's last page, and it is a page about a thing that is not going to be arranged.** Nineteen years in one room, writes the minutes, advises nobody, asks nothing, about four thousand entries in eleven books and not one name in any of them, which is not carelessness and is the only shape a minute book has got, and the window about two feet wide with a pane out of it that has not been put back in about four years. **A man of about sixty-one has come about nine miles to that building twice in nineteen years and both times it was a season, and both times somebody had told a carrier in a lane where to come, and a carrier in a lane is the whole of the instrument, and nobody has ever been told that a man was expected.** **There is no form in this empire for asking a man of sixty-one to walk nine miles so that a clerk can put a hand on the foot of a sheet, and there is no form that would let anybody tell him he is expected, and the two absences are one absence and not two.** The season is on, about nine hundred sheets will go out of that room before the end of it, one of them will go to the district he lives in, and nobody tells him. **She is not going to ask him one question when he comes, and she gave the reason out loud in that room with nobody else in it, to a page: a question put in that building is a question put into a record; the record is nineteen years of a woman of fifty-three copying a hand into a shelf; the sheet goes in there; the last time a thing of that shape happened to about four hundred people their sheet went back; a minute with an answer in it is an order and a clerk of that office has not entered one in nineteen years and there is no form that lets her.** **The question in the second of the eleven books, entered on her own motion, at nobody's request, with the day and the hour on it and her own name at the foot of it, on the fourth day of the third week of the ninth month of the year after next, is still a question. A quarter of it was answered out loud in that room in the second month of last year, by a man who came nine miles on his own feet and told nobody what was said afterwards, and she wrote none of that down either, and nobody is going to ask her a second time.** **Owed and unpaid:** the answer; the fact that she is the only person in this matter answerable in writing for a question and is paid nothing; about four thousand entries with no name in any of them; and the cost of a morning in Chapter 0260, which is that she wrote none of it down, and a price is not a favour. **Her refusal in this batch:** she wrote nothing down this afternoon at all, and she sent no carrier, and she is not going to be thanked and there is no form in this empire for thanking a person for saying a thing at a rail. **Her unanswered question:** hers, in the second of the eleven books, and it is not going to be asked again by anybody, and she said out loud in the third week of the eleventh month that nobody is going to, and nobody is going to.

**Halla Wray, fifty-one, foreman of the Slade Cut — a class, and a box, and two girls at the back of a bay.** **Chapter 0306 is her chapter and nobody asks her anything in it.** She has been in a box since the first week of the seventh month of the year after, entered by a class, and has never been asked about it, and she has worked out in about four minutes, standing at a bench in a bay in the cold, **that being in a box and not being asked about it are the same arrangement, and that the arrangement was made in a shed by nine families and not by her, and that a person inside an arrangement they did not make and are not asked about cannot get out of it by any act of their own.** **The entries that put her where she is were about a class, and a class is a heading, and a heading is how a person becomes a company, and a company is a thing this empire can hold wages against and give letters to and take to law.** She did not say that out loud in a bay to nine men who cannot read a paragraph, and she is not going to say again the thing she said once in a room about the form not asking her whether she would represent anybody and asking who she represents, with a column for the answer and no column for a refusal. About nine men know she is in a box and that is nine mouths and not a document, and not one of the nine has said a word about it since. **At the back of that bay, on a written engagement at the rate a list is set at, a girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are both present in this chapter and neither of them is spoken to, neither is thanked, neither is sent for, and neither is going to start, and the chapter does not say why.** A mark in chalk on a wall at the height of the third link of a chain is a mark and means nothing and is nobody's and is about four years off being anybody's evidence. **Owed and unpaid:** the second sentence a book-keeper four hundred yards up that lane wants and has wanted since the third month of the year after and has not asked for, **and the day he asks is the day she stops saying the half she has got, and nobody asks in this volume**; the form that put her in the box has not been asked to be void by anybody; and the finding that being in a box and not being asked about it are the same arrangement. **Her refusal in this batch:** she did not ask the four who cannot read a paragraph one question about a number, and she did not say the class out loud in the bay, and she did not ask the man of about thirty anything back. **Her unanswered question:** who she represents, which the column took an answer to and no column exists for the refusal.

**Rennick Adley, thirty-eight, book-keeper of the Slade Cut Company — present in this batch only as a debt somebody else owes him.** **He is named in Chapter 0306, at second hand, as the man four hundred yards up that lane who wants the rest of a second sentence and has wanted it since the third month of the year after and has not asked and is not going to.** He keeps a column with no names in it that he built in the second month of next year because a name in a column is a thing a person can be served at, and the days he spends on other people's numbers are not paid and cannot be, and the fourth thing on a fee board about four hundred yards from the counter cannot be accounted for by him or by two other clerks. **Owed and unpaid and untouched by these ten chapters:** the second sentence, and the fact that asking for it is the day she stops, and nobody has asked; about nineteen days' money in a weigh-house ledger; the fourth thing on the fee board; and a mark in chalk on a wall that is about four years from being anybody's evidence. **He is not thanked in this batch and is not spoken to and is not on any list of this batch and the outline does not give him the second sentence and the not-asking is still the volume's finding reached by a different man in a different place and said to nobody.**

**Marn Ottery, thirty-four, a clerk at the fourth counter, eleven years — the volume's first rule, said out loud, and a box under the counter.** **Chapter 0303 is her chapter and it says the whole of it in a room, to nobody in particular, and nobody thanked her for it.** She said the shape of it first, the way she has said the shape of a thing before she has said the thing about nine hundred times in eleven years and the way she has said it to a person twice, and then she said the thing: **a person can say a thing out loud in a room and nothing that any paper in this empire can hold comes of it; a person cannot ask a thing out loud at all, because being asked is being served, and being served is a party, and a party is the only person who can be told what a thing is going to be used for.** A man of about forty-five came up that stair and she did not ask him one thing about the office, the paper, or why he had come. **About four hundred bought and unfilled blanks are under that counter and there is no form anywhere in this empire that lets her keep them, and she has kept them eleven years and she is not going to stop, and the box is not a post and this volume does not revisit the argument about it.** A blank is the only piece of paper in this empire that cannot be held against anybody; a Table is the only place where a person can come up, ask a question, and walk away with a piece of paper that says they asked it; the box is the nearest thing to a post anybody has built and the only thing that would turn it into one is a person asking for it, and a person asking for it is told no by a person, because it would stop on the day the first person with a form wanted it to. She has put a coin back on a counter once in eleven years rather than take it and nobody has asked her to account for that either. **Owed and unpaid:** the answer to a question about a line of writing on the fee board that nobody can answer; the fourth thing on that board that she and two other people cannot account for; about four hundred blanks' worth of nothing; and the price of eleven years of being the person at the counter who does not ask. **Her refusal in this batch:** she did not ask the man of forty-five anything, she did not resolve anything about the box, she did not name a House, and she did not put a name in a column. **Her unanswered question:** whether a counter that a person can come up to stops being that on the day something holds a person there, and she has worked out the answer and has not said it out loud to anybody but the four feet of room she said the rest of it in.

**Nell Kest, twenty, a dye-house worker, sixteen books, a furnace town about four hundred and thirty miles up this river — the other end, and the chapter is careful not to make her the other end of anything else.** **Chapter 0302 is her chapter and she is not told anything and she asks nothing.** She has decided to go and tell four women that she is not paid and has told one, and three are left, and the going is on her own time and there is no fund for the telling and no half-day and nobody to cover the bench. Fifteen of the sixteen books are other people's, none has an office on it, one has her own name at the head of it, **and if somebody came up those two stairs with a sheet and a seal she could not show a soul the fourth of them.** Her wage has been held since the second week of the third month of the year after by a man who cannot say what it is held against, and the money for nineteen days is in a weigh-house ledger with her wage in it and not her name under it. A foreman off a dye end has come up two stairs four times, said the same three things each time, and is holding a wage-day notice in a coat without sending it. She refused money from a woman of about thirty and gave the reason out loud, that if she takes it then she is a trade and a trade can be told what to do and the woman cannot be told what to do and that is the only thing she has got. She is not going up this river this season and has not said she is never going to, and she is the only person who knows there is a difference between the two. **This chapter is the other end of a practice and it does not become the other end: she is not told anything, she is not asked anything, and what she has out loud is a wage held, sixteen books and three women to go. The woman about nine miles off a building off the old river road is a different person, has told a different woman something else, and is kept apart on purpose, and she does not appear in this chapter at all.** **Owed and unpaid:** three of the four women untold; the sixteenth book; a wage held; a man who cannot say what it is held against; and a foreman in a coat with a notice in it. **Her refusal in this batch:** she refused the money, and she told the foreman what to do with the notice instead, and she is not going to be thanked for any of it and has not been. **Her unanswered question:** what it is held against, and nobody in that building can answer it and there is no form in this empire that would carry the question there.

**The woman of about twenty-six at the end of the cold passage — an error in her own head, found in four minutes, and not corrected.** **Chapter 0308 is her chapter and nobody asks her anything and she asks nothing.** She has been in that building about four years, she is not in this matter and has never been in it, and she has counted in her head and without touching the rack the racks that go down that passage and come back light by one, every day at about the third hour, for about four years. The figure has gone up since the seventh month of the year after and she has not said by how much and is not going to, and the figure itself is not printed in any of the ten files of this batch. **What is new in this chapter is that she worked out, in about four minutes this week, that the figure is a count of carriers and not of people — a rack that comes back light by one has a carrier's own in it, and a carrier's own is the carrier's own business and is entered nowhere and is seen by nobody — and that the count of what comes back light is not a count of what is sitting in a room, and that it is very close to one and wrong in a direction she can name and cannot put a figure to, and she is not going to correct it and is not going to hand it to anybody in a state she knows to be wrong.** She has three questions for a man of about sixty-one and has asked none of them and is not going to, and she is the only other person in this matter who knows what he said at the rail, and there is no form anywhere that would let anybody ask her what she heard. **Owed and unpaid:** the figure she will not give and will not hand on; three questions she will not ask; and the third word on the slate, which exists and has no name on it. **Her refusal in this batch:** she did not give the figure, she did not put it in a book, she did not come up the stair, and she did not walk the four hundred yards. **Her unanswered question, which is her own and is not on the page and is not restated in any form that could be put in a mouth:** the second half of this matter's question, which nobody has asked in three hundred and ten files and which this batch did not ask.

**The others, and every debt this batch leaves standing on them, and nothing here is resolved.** **About four men in a bay who cannot read a paragraph, unnamed, still never asked one question about a number in any of the six closed volumes and in none of these ten chapters, and the man of about fifty-five with a chain among them is not one of them and says so and is not put with them.** The reader of seventeen at the back of that bay on a written engagement at the rate a list is set at, unnamed, unspoken to, unthanked, unsent for, not going to start. The girl of seventeen in the same bay, in the same condition, who would say yes and has never been given the chance to say no, and a chapter that thanks her breaks this batch and no chapter of it did. A man of about thirty from the second gang, a party, who asked a man of thirty-eight what his being in a room left him with and was told he was left with three more things than he had that morning, and who is not spoken to in these ten chapters. A man of about thirty with fourpence in his hand who did not spend it. A man of about forty-four. A man of about thirty-four who came four miles in the rain and could not finish a question and did not come back. A woman of about thirty-five with a day-book in a lodging house who came about nine miles twice, was not let in, and wrote none of it down. A woman of about forty with a scuttle who lit a lamp early once and is not in this matter and cannot be asked what she heard, and who lit a lamp early in Chapter 0301 as she does twice a week. A woman of about thirty who has money and offered some of it and was refused. A boy of about nine with two slates, the second one with the office question on it and no name on it, and nobody has thanked him and nobody ever has. A foreman off a dye end holding a notice in a coat. About nine men who know a foreman of fifty-one is in a box. **The man of about thirty-four's wife, unnamed, not thanked, has not been thanked, did not ask him how the week went, and said out loud some weeks ago that she is not going to. The two documents stay two documents, four hundred and thirty miles apart, and neither is named in any of these ten files. And two boxes that stay shut, a guarantee that stands unanswered with about sixty children inside it and no child named in it, and a bill at nineteen pounds three and fourpence that nobody is liable for.**

## VOLUME 09 — THE PEOPLE A VOLUME 09 WRITER INHERITS AT CHAPTER 0400, AND WHAT EACH OF THEM IS STILL REFUSED, AND THE FOUR DEBTS RESTATED IN FULL

*Appended downward by the close of Volume 08. **Nothing above this point is rewritten.** This is a handoff and it is not a plan: **`outline/volume-09.md` did not exist when this line was written, and it exists now**, and the wrong claim is named here and deleted nowhere. **It is 111,429 bytes across 265 lines, it is titled *The Blank*, it is the outline of record for Chapters 0401 to 0450, and it was written by the phase at `workspace/volume-09/volume-09-outline/` and amended once by the repair that took `logs/volume-09-outline.review.log`. A writer who reaches this section has therefore inherited the people and the volume both, and the sentence this one carried — that a volume cannot be planned from a plan and the phase that plans Volume 09 comes before any batch of it — has been satisfied and the batch is running.** The series plan in `outline/series.md` gives Volume 09 a coalition, a convention, a charter and a named antagonist's offer, and **the page has none of those and has never had them; read that block as a plan the series holds and not as a description of a world this manuscript has built**, and read `outline/volume-09.md`'s own declarations, which refuse that block field by field including its title, before you read a card. The ending of record is unchanged: Volume 12, and the final image is still an ordinary local hearing in which a child receives two copies of a record and learns that a debt can be heard, limited, and refused.*

**Marek Kest, thirty-eight, the protagonist, and the standing instruction about him that is this volume's floor and not a plan of entrances.** He holds nothing: no office, no fund, no list, no leave, no stage, no certification at any point in eight volumes. He refuses the reading, does not exercise the thing he is able to do, and is not at a stage and is not going to arrive at one. **His want is the erased name of his mother and the disputed family claim, and it is not resolved, and the name is not printed, and the name of the hand that struck the line is not printed either, and the who is Volume 06's and goes on unanswered.** `outline/volume-08.md` set the floor at three chapters a movement, in person or as a person whose absence has a named cost in the room he is not in, and his want visible in at least one chapter of every movement, and the volume met it in three movements of five and missed it in two. **The finding that came with the floor is that a protagonist put in a room that is not his is the same defect as a chapter with nobody in it, and a count is not an answer to it: in person he stood in six of the volume's fifty chapters, not four as this section first printed it — 0355, 0365, 0371, 0379, 0390 and 0399, one in each movement except Movement Three, which has two — and the wrong figure is named and not deleted.** Nobody asked him anything, nobody thanked him, and the woman about four miles off at the top of a stair is still not told that he said a reason out loud to about nine men in a bay. **His reason for not reaching a stage is in about nine words on a page and may not be paid a second time, and the labour he chose out of his own hand is not re-decided.**

**Tamsin Rook, twenty-four, at the fourth counter, two years, and the person the volume closed on.** Nobody has ever put a question to her in that time and that is her whole position. Her undertaking of the fourth of the first month is live, unretired and unexercised, and its date is not said out loud and is not said out loud by a state record either. **She is ready and has not been told what she is standing ready for, and one colleague knows it, and readiness is not a form and cannot be entered on anything.** She took her apron off the hook and hung it up again at a quarter past the fourth hour in the last chapter, because she had come in twenty minutes early for two years and there had been no need to. **A Volume 09 writer may not turn her into an organiser, a clerk with a title, a person who has been given a post, or a person somebody has finally asked; the series plan's own relationship field for this volume says she becomes an accountable organizer and that is a series plan and not this page, and the decision about whether she trusts a colleague's judgment is unmade, is not on the page, and may not be made in a state file.**

**Marn Ottery, thirty-four, at the other end of that counter, eleven years, not a lawyer.** About four hundred bought and unfilled blanks under the boards, unopened in six years, three inches further forward than they stood ten weeks ago. She has said the shape of a thing out loud in that room three times and been asked nothing. **Her want, which the state layer has never printed plainly and printed once in this file's close section: that the two women at that counter go on being the only two who know what is in that drawer, and that the arrangement that makes that true keeps standing.** She is not thanked, and in the last chapter she enters in terms that she is not going to be thanked.

**Nell Kest, twenty, about four hundred and thirty miles up this river, in a counting room at the back of a dye end.** Sixteen volumes, fifteen borrowed, the one with her own name in capitals unopened. Nineteen days of a crew's money in a coat four miles off and a notice with a printed ruled space in the same pocket with the space clean. **She is not going to ask what it is held against, and nobody paid her, sent for her, thanked her or forgave her, and the rule a woman said to her once in a lane has not been given to a third woman, and she is not going up this river this season and a season is not a life.** She is not the woman of about twenty-six and not the woman who keeps a rented house's ground floor and not the clerk of about fifty-three, and no Volume 09 chapter may put any two of them in one room.

**Halla Wray, fifty-one, a foreman at the Slade end, in a box entered by a class, which is a heading.** The form that would take the two of seventeen at the back of that shed out of the back of it is still on the board and will be on it again on the second of the two days next week, and **the form that put her where she is is not asked to be void by anybody, because nothing in this empire has ever been asked to be void and there is no procedure for asking.** The two of seventeen are still on that bench, the girl is still not given the chance to say no, the reader of seventeen is still unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for, the man of about fifty-five with the chain is not one of the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph and never is, and the second half of the sentence she began in a doorway has still not arrived.

**Rennick Adley, thirty-eight, the Company's book-keeper, four hundred yards up the lane off the Slade.** Wants the rest of a sentence and has not asked and is not going to. He wrote the same four lines out for the eleventh time and they came out the same. The clerk of about twenty-nine told him out loud that a box entered by a class does not come out of itself and that there is nobody he could tell and no form for telling. **The four hundred yards is not walked and is not to be walked to close a scene.**

**The man of about thirty-four with the fair hand.** The only person in this matter anybody could put a question to and the one nobody has. A number in his head that has never been written and never passed on, and a form with a printed heading over a ruled space that came through his letter slot and was not returned. He has put the not knocking on the woman next door because he has nobody he could hand it to. **The next asking is his and it is nobody's yet, and no chapter may make it anybody's, and the number is not to be printed, confirmed or denied.**

**The man of about sixty-one, the second hand since he was forty-two, who cannot read a paragraph.** About nine hundred sheets a year, about nine of them not what the person above him wrote, every one of them signed by him, and he is the only person alive who knows which and cannot write one down. A second true thing was said to be coming in about four months by a young man paid by the corner, and it did not arrive, and the nine miles is not walked. **He is neither of the two women in their boxes and is not one of the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph, and no Volume 09 chapter may merge him with either group.**

**The clerk of about fifty-three, nineteen years in one room off the old river road.** Writes the minutes, advises nobody, asks nothing. Her own finding is on a shelf under a window with no pane in it, a question with no full stop and her own name at the foot, and **she is the only person in this matter anybody could serve a question on in writing.** She said one true thing out loud in Chapter 0392 that was about the weather and the only other person in that room wrote none of it down. **Her question stays a question, carries no period, and its author is not asked a second time.**

**The woman of about twenty-six at the lock end of about four hundred yards of cold flags.** Four years at that lock, never sent for, thanked or handed a sheet. A figure in her head that is on no paper, has gone up, is not handed on and **does not get a heading**. **She stands at the lock and the room with the rail is at the other end of those same four hundred yards and is not hers; the rail has nothing on it and has not had anything on it since before she came, which is 0393's third line and 0358's title, and the room at that far end is entered twice a week by the woman of about forty with a scuttle. The four hundred yards is not walked and the two women are never in one room.** Two claims in this row were false against the page and are named here and deleted nowhere: it said she was at the end of that passage, and it said the room at the far end of those flags was not entered. The first put her in the other woman's room, which is a merge this project has spent a volume preventing. **Two section headings higher up this file still call her the woman of about twenty-six at the end of the cold passage, and they are left exactly as they stand, because this file's own rule is that nothing above the Volume 09 handoff marker is rewritten and a correction that breaks a standing rule to fix a phrase that a reader meets once in a heading is a worse trade than the phrase.**

**The woman of about thirty-five next door, the woman of about forty with a scuttle, the woman of about thirty-five with a day-book, the woman of about twenty-two in her second season, the woman of about nineteen who keeps minutes under the clerk, the clerk of about twenty-nine at the other end of two joined tables, the woman who keeps a rented house's ground floor, and the man in the felt apron.** Each is a person and not a device and each is named by age and none of them is a type. **The claim that stood here, that the woman of about forty with a scuttle is in none of Volume 08's fifty files, was false against the page and is named here and deleted nowhere. She is in fourteen of the four hundred closed chapter files — 0296, 0297 and 0300 in Volume 06, 0301, 0307, 0312, 0320, 0321, 0323, 0324, 0336, 0340 and 0346 in Volume 07, and Chapter 0362 in Volume 08, whose title is *The End Of Four Hundred Yards Of Cold Flags, A Lamp, And A Woman Of Forty Nobody Can Ask* and which is set in the room with the rail from its first paragraph to its last.** The page gives her a week and no more: the passage twice a week with a scuttle and a lamp and a cloth, and a washhouse two streets off on the other day, and her own sentence that the two halves of her week are not the same trade and are not the same woman. **A Volume 09 writer may not give her a room, a trade, a week or a history the page has not given her, may not discover her where she was not, and Chapter 0362 is where she was and is the only Volume 08 chapter she is in. She is not the woman of about twenty-six and no chapter may put the two in one room.**

### The four debts, restated in full at the Volume 08 close, and this close discharges none of them

**One: an owed review of Volume 04's Batch 0005, four volumes on. Two, three and four: owed second readings of Volume 05's Batches 0003, 0004 and 0005 and of Volume 06's own Batch 0003, which is four and not three.** Plus the review gate, which opened and produced findings on all seven Batch 0005 phases the commit history records, and has fallen back to the writing agent every time it has been asked, and has never once produced a review that could be certified independent, **and a gate that only ever falls back is not a gate that passed either**, and the open items that are not plot, with the sentence bound among them, which are now eighty-nine and whose numbering is not a run, since forty-nine and fifty are absent from the ledger along with items 18 to 33 and 35 to 42, and the live ledger holds sixty-three entries against a high-water mark of eighty-nine. **The number of debts has not moved in eight volumes and the number of phases that have claimed to discharge one is zero. A close is where a debt is most likely to be quietly dropped, because a close feels like a finish, and this section restates all four in full for a Volume 09 writer and discharges none of them, and a Volume 09 writer who inherits a ledger of eighty-nine open items and no debt has been misinformed by somebody.**

# THE HANDOFF VERIFICATION BETWEEN VOLUME 08 AND VOLUME 09 — THE PEOPLE AT FOUR HUNDRED CHAPTERS, RE-DERIVED, AND WHAT THIS PHASE CHANGED ABOUT THEM, WHICH IS ONE CHECK AND NOBODY

*Appended downward by the phase that took `workspace/volume-09/volume-09-handoff/PROMPT.md`, after the close of Volume 08 and after the review repair of that close. **Nothing above this point is rewritten and no status about any person above is changed.** The Volume 08 sections of this file were moved verbatim to `state/archive/rolling-volume-08-records.md` and a pointer stands above them; the Volume 09 handoff section below the pointer is the one roster a Volume 09 writer opens first, and the consolidated roster at the close of Volume 05 stayed above the pointer because it is the base later changes are measured from. **This phase opened no chapter, wrote no prose, and did not write `outline/volume-09.md`.***

**Nobody in this matter moved, and that is the finding and not a gap.** Every person listed in the Volume 09 handoff section above this one stands exactly as the close of Volume 08 and its review repair left them, and this phase re-derived the two figures that are about people rather than about the page and found both of them correct. **It is entered here because a handoff that reports no change has to say that it looked, and a record that says nothing happened and does not say what was checked is indistinguishable from a record that did not check.**

**Marek Kest is in person in six of Volume 08's fifty chapters, not four.** 0355 in Movement One, 0365 in Movement Two, 0371 and 0379 in Movement Three, 0390 in Movement Four, 0399 in Movement Five — one in each movement except Movement Three, which has two. The other five of the eleven chapters the floor counts are absences with a cost named in somebody else's mouth: 0377, 0382, 0385, 0392 and 0398. **Both figures were re-derived by this phase from the fifty files and both reproduce, and the close's figure of four in person is named and not deleted.**

**And the finding is about the check, and it is new, and it is the reason a handoff is worth running.** **The protagonist's presence cannot be counted off a string in this matter, because both obvious strings are carried by other living people who are not merges.** A sweep for his surname returns eleven files and **five of the eleven are his sister Nell**, who is a person of the volume with sixteen volumes and a wage held in a coat four miles off. A sweep for a man of thirty-eight returns **thirteen** files, six of which also carry the surname, so seven of them name a man of thirty-eight without it, and **two of those seven are Rennick Adley, the Company's book-keeper, who is also thirty-eight and who wants the rest of a sentence and has not asked, and who is a different man four hundred yards up the same lane** — one naming him outright, 0381, and one describing him as the man who keeps that Company's books four hundred yards up that lane, 0386. The other five are the protagonist described and not named. The union of the two sweeps is **eighteen**, and the correct figure is eleven by the floor's definition and six in person, eighteen being wrong by exactly the seven files that carry one of the two strings without carrying him. **So any check that reads this man's presence off a name or an age overcounts him, and it would have overcounted him in every volume, and it is not a question of care: a name and an age are exactly the strings a check can see, and the sister who carries the name and the book-keeper who carries the age are on the page and are never merged with him in any sentence. Chapter 0398 is the file that shows what a sweep cannot do, being Adley's chapter with Adley named in the room and the protagonist put into a clerk's mouth in it, and it carries the surname nowhere at all, so the age sweep reaches it and the surname sweep does not: the three files 0381, 0386 and 0398 differ by nothing a string can see, only by what the man standing in the room says.**

**This is the standing for the Volume 09 floor, and the floor must not be counted by string.** A floor stated as a number can be met by a sentence in somebody else's mouth, which is item 87's finding, and a floor counted by a name or an age can be met by his sister and by a book-keeper, which is this one. **A Volume 09 outline that sets a floor of three a movement and verifies it by searching for the protagonist's name will pass on a page where he is not in the room, and a search for a man of thirty-eight will pass on a page where a different man is.**

**Nothing else about him moved and nothing about anybody else moved.** He holds nothing: no office, no fund, no list, no leave, no stage, no certification at any point in eight volumes. He refuses the reading and does not exercise the thing he is able to do, and his reason for not reaching a stage is in about nine words on the page and is not paid a second time, and the labour he chose out of his own hand is not re-decided. His want — the erased name of his mother and the disputed family claim — is unresolved, the name of the hand that struck the line out of the leaf in his coat is in his head and on no paper, and unanswered is not the same as closed. **Nobody asked him one thing, nobody thanked him, nobody forgave him and nobody sent for him, and the count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven and did not move.**

**The separations hold and this phase broke none of them.** A man of about sixty-one is nine miles off a building off the old river road and is neither of the two women in their boxes. A woman of about twenty-six is at the lock of a cold passage nine miles off the lane off the Slade and is a third person. A woman of twenty is about four hundred and thirty miles up this river in a furnace town. **And the woman who keeps the ground floor of the rented house is not the clerk of about fifty-three, and the woman of about forty with a scuttle is not the woman of about twenty-six, and no two of the three people kept apart at that address are in one room in any file of Volume 08 and none may be in one in Volume 09.** **Two claims in this paragraph were false against the page and are named here and deleted nowhere. It said the woman of about twenty-six was at the end of that passage: she is at the lock, and the room with the rail at the other end of it is not hers. And it said the woman of about forty with a scuttle is in none of Volume 08's fifty files: she is in Chapter 0362, which is named for her, and in thirteen files before it. What survives of the second instruction is the part that was always the point, that a Volume 09 writer may not give her a room, a trade, a week or a history the page has not given her, and may not discover her where she was not.**

**And the four debts, restated in full here for the tenth time, and this phase discharges none of them.** An owed review of Volume 04's Batch 0005, four volumes on. Owed second readings of Volume 05's Batches 0003, 0004 and 0005 and of Volume 06's own Batch 0003, which is four and not three. The review gate, which opened and produced findings on all seven Batch 0005 phases the commit history records, has fallen back to the writing agent every time it has been asked, has never once produced a review that could be certified independent, **and a gate that only ever falls back is not a gate that passed either.** And the open items that are not plot, with the sentence bound among them, which are now eighty-nine by the high-water mark, **eighty-seven entries measured in the rolling ledger before the eighth enforcement and three in it now, and the sixty-three this project has been quoting is twenty-four short, which is item 90.** **A handoff verification wrote the files the Volume 09 outline will be built on and no hand other than the one that wrote them has read them, so the third debt now has a fourth instance and the number of instances is not a measure of the debt. The number of debts has not moved in eight volumes and the number of phases that have claimed to discharge one is zero, and this phase is not among them.**

Nothing was deleted, summarised, condensed or paraphrased, and every figure inside the moved sections stands as the run that wrote it measured it at the time.**
*Appended downward by the review repair of `logs/batch-0005.review.log`. **No character fact above is altered by this repair. No character was given a new room, a new trade, a new week, a new history, a new line or a new decision, no two characters were merged, and no character was split. Every edit this repair made to the ten chapters was to wording. What follows is the short list of places where a reader of the entries above would find that the repair changed what a character SAYS and not what a character IS, and that is the whole of the change and it is worth naming because a reword that changes a character's grammar can change what a reader thinks they were refusing.***

## The four rewordings that touched a mouth, and what was kept in each

**The man of about thirty-four with the fair hand, in 0448.** **The exchange that re-printed 0437's — a different man, in a different room, saying *You are not going to ask me for it* and being told *I am not going to ask you for it* — is now about the inside pocket of the coat.** The two men are the same two men, the scene is the same scene, the paper is still on the table against the base of the wall, **and the refusal is the same refusal, because he is still not going to be the man who takes it and Marek Kest still did not ask.** What changed is what they decline to discuss: it was an unplaced *it* and it is now a coat with a folded leaf in it, **and the character fact that a man says a true thing out loud before he is asked for it is untouched and is the third of the three in that room, and the number in his head is still in no mouth and was neither confirmed nor denied.** What is also untouched: he did not come in, he was not thanked, nobody was sent for, and the sentence about the gap at the foot of a sheet still stands in his own words with the figure the calendar supports.

**The man of about twenty-six who is paid by the corner, in 0441 and 0447.** **Two of his lines were reworded and neither was softened.** The line that said *I am not going to be thanked for it* now says *nobody is going to thank me for the carrying of it either*, which is the same refusal in a sentence that had to be split because the reword carried it past the ceiling. **The line that said *You did not ask me and I am not going to stand here and say that you did not* now says that standing there saying she did not ask is the last thing he is going to do with his morning** — and the standing is what it was, and he still went down those stairs with the box, and he still went down them twice more, and he still bought a piece of paper with nothing printed on it with fourpence and carried it in his hand and did not fill it in. **He is still not going to be findable, he still has not said where the paper is now, and the ten nouns that keep him apart from the man of about thirty-four are re-ordered and not removed.**

**The man of about sixty-one, in 0442.** **The one new thing about him in this movement is the second mark on a sheet, and it is untouched.** What was reworded is the *reporting* of him: his pen going back into the pot, the hook emptying, and the young man's leaving. **He still cannot read a paragraph, he still did not look up, he still has nowhere to write a thing down, and he is still not in a bay with anybody, and the two words he did not finish are still the two words he did not finish.**

**Tamsin Rook, twenty-four, in 0449.** **Her finding is untouched and it is still hers and it is still not in a mouth: that a person with something behind her is not available, and that the practice has never once gone looking for one, and the reason.** What was reworded is her *refusal to give it away* — the line that said *I am going to say one thing and then I am going to put my hands back on this boards* now says there is one thing coming and then her hands are going back, and the reason sentence was restructured and says the same four things: she will not say it in that room, she will not say it out of it, nobody is going to thank her for working it out, and nobody is going to ask her for it. **She is still twenty-four, still at the fourth counter, still not a lawyer, still has an undertaking that is live and unused and is not going to be used, and she still said nothing this week that is going to cost her, and she was still not thanked for the nothing, and there is still no form in which she could be.**

**And the four characters the repair did not put a word in.** Marek Kest, who is thirty-eight and holds nothing and was in the room in 0447, 0448 and 0450 and asked nothing; the man of about fifty-five with the chain; the woman who keeps the ground floor of a rented house, **who still has not gone up the four steps and never is going to and whose twenty years are still twenty years**; the man who is paid for a corner is still not the young man from the shipping floor, and the young man is still carrying a piece of paper in a coat about four miles off, and the man of about fifty-five with the chain and the man of about sixty-one are still neither of them one of the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph. **A merge does not need two rooms to happen, it needs two people and one mouth, and this repair put no sentence in any mouth that a reader could not already tell the speakers of.**

# THE CLOSE OF VOLUME 09 — THE PEOPLE AT FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY CHAPTERS, AND THE ONE FINDING ABOUT THEM THAT IS NOT ABOUT A PERSON

*Appended downward by the phase that took `workspace/volume-09/volume-close/PROMPT.md`. The full close is in `state/archive/volume-09-close.md`. **No character fact above this point is altered by this section and no person is merged with anybody, because a merge does not need two rooms to happen, it needs two people and one mouth.***

**Marek Kest, thirty-eight, the protagonist.** He holds nothing, he is not at a stage, he refuses the reading, and he is on the page by name in eleven of Volume 09's fifty chapters: 0404, 0407, 0409, 0413, 0417, 0420, 0425, 0434, 0447, 0448 and 0450. **The string *thirty-eight* is on the page in thirteen of them and the two extra are 0405, 0406 and 0433, which are Rennick Adley, and 0410, which is a woman of about thirty-eight with fourpence and a blank in her coat — a check that reads a person off a string cannot tell a man from a woman with a name for money in her hand.** His want — the name struck out at the end of a line, in a hand that is not his mother's, and the claim that went with it — is visible in 0404, 0425, 0434, 0448 and 0450, and the name is in no mouth and the hand that struck it is in no mouth. **He gained a paper and no office and no stage and no second copy of anything, and nobody sent it and nobody thanked him, and his reason for not reaching a stage is not paid a second time in any of the fifty.**

**The finding about him, and it is the one this close found and it is about the check and not about the man: the outline of record's floor — three chapters a movement, in person in two of the three, the want visible in one — is met in two movements of five.** Counted by movement: three named and three in person in Movement One; three named and one in person in Movement Two; one named in Movement Three; one named in Movement Four; three named and three in person in Movement Five. **Three state records print that floor as met exactly and not by one, and one of them prints the reason, which is that in two of its three chapters the protagonist is neither named nor given an age — and this close read both of those chapters and the man in neither is Marek Kest.** Chapter 0422's man came up four flights with nothing in his hands and is unnamed, and 0407 numbers the same act *the second time in his life* and 0440 numbers it *the third time*, and 0422 is counted by neither. Chapter 0428's woman has known a tenant of her stair for nine years and has chosen nine times a year not to say what he is, and Marek Kest has been in his room two years, and that chapter's own fifth line says its woman is not the clerk of about fifty-three. **The floor is carried unrepaired and is a finding about a check that was run five times, once a movement, on ten files at a time, and passed five times.**

**Rennick Adley, thirty-eight, the book-keeper of about nine hundred rooms.** He is not Marek Kest and the page holds them apart, and the clause that does it is on the page in both directions: *he is paid for a corner and not for a page* is the man of about twenty-six, and *he cannot read a paragraph* is the man of about sixty-one, and *he can read a paragraph and has always been able to read a paragraph* is the man of about fifty-five, and **the two of the three that are thirty-eight are the protagonist and the book-keeper, and the two strings that identify them are the same age, which is why the floor had to be counted by reading and not by a string.** He wants the rest of a sentence a woman of fifty-one stopped giving him in a doorway in a month that is gone, and the ruled space under the four lines has wanted dates since the first month and has never once become a question.

**Tamsin Rook, twenty-four, at the near end of those boards, two years, and the finding of the last movement is hers and is still not in a mouth.** Her undertaking is live, unretired and unexercised and its date is not said out loud. **She was handed a blank at 0424, a man came up the four flights and bought nothing at 0440, and a man of about thirty-four with a fair hand put a piece of paper with nothing printed on it on her table in 0447 and stood it against four feet of bare wall in 0449 and came back with nothing in his hands in 0450 and would not be thanked and would not come a third time.** She knows what she is standing ready for and the decision about whether she trusts a colleague's judgment is unmade and is not made in any of the fifty chapters.

**The woman of about forty with a scuttle is in fourteen of the four hundred closed files and Chapter 0362 is named for her, and Volume 09 put her in no chapter at all, and this close gives her no room, no trade, no week and no history the page has not given her.**

**And the four debts, restated in full, and this close discharges none of them, and it changed no character's fact.**

# THE VOLUME 09 HANDOFF: WHAT THE PAGE SAYS ABOUT EVERY PERSON, AND THE TWO FIGURES THAT WERE WRONG

*Written by the phase that took `workspace/volume-10/volume-10-handoff/PROMPT.md`. No character's fact was changed, no chapter opened for edit, and no merge made or refused here. Every entry was read out of the fifty files of Volume 09 or measured across them.*

**Marek Kest, thirty-eight.** In person in **ten** chapters of Volume 09, being 0404, 0407, 0409, 0417, 0420, 0425, 0434, 0447, 0448 and 0450, and named in a mouth and not in the room in one, being 0413, where Tamsin Rook says at the counter *Marek Kest is the name on him*. **The close record counted nine chapters in person and missed 0420, and the correct figure is ten, and the ten are printed here and the nine are named and not deleted.** He holds nothing: no office, no fund, no list, no leave, no certification, and none of the five is on its way. He is not at a stage and is not going to arrive at one. His want is a leaf in the inside pocket of a coat, struck through by a hand that is not his mother's, carried about two years, and it is visible at 0404, 0417, 0420, 0425, 0434 and 0448 and in no other chapter. He came up those four flights three times and bought nothing. **He is not Rennick Adley, who is thirty-eight and is a different man, and Adley is at 0405, 0406 and 0433. He is not the tenant of a rented house's stair with about nine years of rent behind a boiler, and that man is never named. He is not the unnamed man who came up those four flights at the fourth hour and went back down them at 0422, who is unnamed and unaged and is described from outside, and the ordinals on the page do not close and are carried unrepaired on purpose.** He refused gratitude at 0450 on the ground that gratitude is a thing that has to be agreed at both ends of it, and he is not going to come a third time.

**Tamsin Rook, twenty-four.** At the counter at the top of four flights, in at twenty minutes to the fifth every working day, which she has done for about seventeen weeks as Chapter 0440 gives it and for about six weeks as Chapter 0424 gives it, **and both figures are on the page and they do not agree and neither is repaired, because a repair that chooses a week is a guess and this project has already made three.** Her undertaking is live, unretired and unexercised, and its date has not been said out loud in two years. She worked out that a person with something behind her is not available and said it to nobody, and at 0449:35 she says *nobody is going to thank me for the working of it and nobody is going to ask me for it either*. At 0440:13 she is said to have spoken once in the second week of the ninth month and once in the fourth week, **and both of those chapters show her saying nothing — 0428 is a different building entirely and 0430:35 has *Tamsin Rook did not move and did not say anything and nobody asked her for a word* — and the finding stands and the sentence is carried unrepaired.** **She is not the clerk of about fifty-three, and Chapter 0428 says so in its own fifth line, and no two of the three women at these addresses may ever be in one room.**

**The man of about twenty-six who is paid by the corner.** He carried the box about four miles on its side in 0443 and is the only person alive who has had both the lid and the eleven years in the same hand. He said one thing to the courier from the yard and went on. **His own closed chapter contradicts itself about his gender and is carried unrepaired on purpose, and he is not the young man from the shipping floor, who is a separate person who put a filled-in sheet inside a coat four miles off.**

**The man of about sixty-one.** Nineteen years at the foot of about nine hundred sheets a year, about nine of which a year are not what the person above him wrote, and he cannot read a paragraph and has never once pretended to. He has said one thing to the pen pot four times in the whole manuscript, at 0396, 0415, 0427 and 0431, and at 0431 he says it is the fourth and the first three were his own, and at 0427 he says it is the third and the other two are from closed Chapter 0396, **and 0415 is the occasion 0427 does not account for, and the four are countable and the two statements differ by one occasion and both are carried unrepaired.** His two figures are not printed, not confirmed and not denied.

**Marn Ottery, thirty-four.** Eleven years at those boards, and the only person on that floor who can say what a piece of paper with nothing printed on it is for, and she said it out loud once and nobody thanked her and she said in terms that she was not going to be. **She says at 0410:19 that the box is not the supply, and the outline of record says it is the only supply, and the page is right and the outline is closed and the contradiction is named and not repaired.** The fourth item on the wall board is in her own hand, is about four years old, and none of the three of them can account for it.

**The clerk of about twenty-nine.** One thing said in that room in about four years, and the reason was given at the sixth hour, and there will not be a second thing about it. **The minute clerk is a different woman and the outline of record gives her the wrong age, and the string *fifty-five* on Volume 09's page is six occurrences and every one of them is the man with the chain, who is not the clerk and is not her.**

**The man of about fifty-five with the chain.** He can read a paragraph and has always been able to read a paragraph, and he is in no room with the four men who cannot get the sense of one. The chain is across the front of the front bench of a shed about nine foot by eleven at the end of a lane off the Slade, and the lamp is not lit until about the seventh hour, and the form on the board by the door has been read by about nobody in that lane for four years.

## THE REPAIR OF THE VOLUME 09 HANDOFF VERIFICATION, WHAT IT CORRECTED, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY LEFT

*Written by the phase that read `logs/volume-09-handoff.review.log` and applied the reading. **This is a repair record and not a review, not a close and not a second reading, and it discharges none of the four debts.** The whole of it is in `reviews/volume-09-handoff.md`, which is the file a Volume 09 planner should open before the state layer and not after it. **No chapter of any volume was opened, no prose was written, and `outline/volume-08.md`, `outline/series.md` and `outline/ending.md` were not opened. The ending of record is unchanged at Volume 12, the final image is unchanged, and no final enemy has been introduced.** Item 43 is a debt and not a figure and it was not touched.

**Six findings, three of them blockers, and the consolidation they were aimed at was sound.** Every word count reproduces to the word; all 1,819 lines removed from the five rolling files are byte-present in the four archive files; 671,539 plus 106,082 is 777,621 exactly; item 90's ledger finding holds against the pre-move file; the forty-six-week calendar finding reproduces out of the fifty date lines; the four question marks, the zero *Lowcross*, the absence of month and weekday names and the eleven-and-six protagonist columns are all right; no controller file and no `outline/` file was touched; and the six rolling files came off a bound they had been over for three volumes. **Nothing in the consolidation was undone, and the two archive files are unedited.**

**What was wrong was arithmetic, in the three places this project has now found seven times running, and in the phase whose own written lesson is the sentence above.** A union of two sweeps was published as **seventeen** and measures, over the fifty files, at `grep -l 'Kest'` = 11 and `grep -l 'thirty-eight'` = 13, six of them carrying both, so **eighteen**. A sweep for a man of thirty-eight was published as **seven** and was never run: seven is a real category — the thirteen less the six that also carry the surname — and **two** of those seven are Rennick Adley and are not the protagonist's chapters, being 0381 by name and 0386 by description, where the record named one. And a ledger count of **eighty-seven** was published as true after the consolidation that emptied the file, where the same command run on the live file today returns **three**, being items 43, 44 and 90, of which only 43 and 44 were in the file before, and with the other eighty-five in the `state/open-threads.md` block of `state/archive/rolling-volume-08-records.md`.

**The arithmetic that makes all three checkable, and it is the finding and not the corrections: eighteen less the five files that name nobody but his sister Nell, less 0381 and 0386, is the eleven the floor counts and the six the volume puts him in person.** The union was not wrong by one. It was wrong by exactly the seven files that carry one of the two strings without carrying the man, and **Chapter 0398 is the file that shows what no sweep can do — it carries the surname nowhere at all, it is Adley's chapter with Adley named in the room, and the man of thirty-eight in it is the protagonist in a clerk's mouth, so the age sweep is right there and wrong in 0381 and 0386, the surname sweep never touches it, and the three differ by nothing a string can see.** So the check is not noisy around a right answer. It is wrong in a way nobody could have predicted, and the repair that corrected the drift got this file wrong on its first pass and was caught by the only check that could catch it, which is that the subtraction has to reproduce the eleven. That sentence is now in the prompt, in the live header, in the character state and in the continuity record, because a Volume 09 writer about to write a floor needs the second kind and not the first.

**The fourth finding is the one this register should keep, and it is not a figure.** `workspace/volume-09/volume-09-outline/PROMPT.md` printed the Lowcross figure in section Two and forbade printing it in section Six, in a document whose entire product is rules and which a Volume 09 planner inherits and has to adjudicate. **The figure is gone and the three facts an outline needs about that bill are in its place, all three of which were in the sentence being cut.** The reading also held that the prompt broke the same prohibition by printing *about nine of about nine hundred a year*, and that is wrong: those are the second hand's annual sheets, they are canon, they are printed openly in six state files and in the outline of record, and the figure section Six forbids under that wording is the number the man with the fair hand keeps in his head, which the prompt nowhere prints. **The defect is therefore not a broken rule but an unreadable one, and the repair says so and names the prohibition's holder instead of the number, because a prohibition a reader has to guess at is half a prohibition and this register has now found that twice — the merge in Chapter 0399, and this.**

**What it did not do, entered so a later reader does not read this section as a plot change.** It did not close an item, discharge a debt, resolve a thread, walk either road or the four hundred yards, thank, forgive or send for anybody, name a House, a seat or an office, print the who's name, the name at the end of a struck line, the name of the hand that struck it, the number in a man's head, or the figure at the end of the cold passage. It did not fill in a ruled space, turn a day-book round, rule a fifth column, date a coming, or find the form of a shed void. It did not correct in place the six records that quote sixty-three, for the reason item 90 itself gives, and a corrected figure that is not named is a figure that gets corrected twice. **Every wrong figure this repair replaced is named beside the right one in the file that carried it and is deleted nowhere**, which includes the union of seventeen, the age sweep of seven, the single Adley file and the eighty-seven that was printed as an after.

**And one hazard for the verifier that comes next, entered because this one paid for it twice.** Two of the review's own first three attempts to measure the archive blocks in `state/archive/rolling-volume-08-records.md` returned figures that were wrong by between 22 and 33 bytes, and the cause is that a block in that file ends with a blank line, then `---`, then a blank line, then `---`, then a blank line, so any method that strips trailing separators once gets a different answer from one that strips them in a loop. **The right figures were right and the wrong ones were transient; the difference between the two is a loop, and a verifier who does not know that will report a defect that is not there.**

**The standing lesson, in its thirtieth consecutive record, and the tenth reading to find the same thing: a figure that was measured by a string is a figure that measured the string, and a figure that was measured against a file is a figure that expires when the file changes.** Both errors were made in one phase, in the sentences that argue against both errors, and the second of them was made by writing down a morning's measurement in an afternoon's sentence. **Run the thing. Then write what you ran. Then say what it cannot see. Then say what state the thing was in, and say again what state it is in now.**

## Volume 09 Batch 0005, Chapters 0441 to 0450, Movement Five, the climax, and it is a chapter batch and not a review, not a self-audit, not a second reading, not a close and not a repair, and it discharged none of the four debts

**The volume's fifty chapters are written. This is the last batch of the volume and the next phase is the close of the volume, and the close is a phase of its own and this section is not it.** The header in `state/current.md` has been amended in place and the header line it replaces is quoted verbatim there and is deleted nowhere.

### What the movement is, in one paragraph, and what the outline of record asked for that the page would not give it

**The box came out from under the end of the boards, went down four flights and about four miles in a carrier's two hands, and was set down on the floor of a room on a second floor and was not opened. In the fourth week of the same month, in the last week of the seventh named year, a man of about sixty-one signed the same sheet twice because nobody told him he had already. In the third week of the first month of the eighth named year, that box went four miles. A man came up a lane about a book and did not get one. A man went up a stair in a rented house who is not the man whose rent it is, and the woman at the bottom of those stairs did not follow him. In the first week of the second month a piece of paper with nothing printed on it was put on a table in the room taken by the week, and nobody sent it, and in the second week it was stood against the base of about four feet of bare wall where he can see it, and in the fourth week the man who brought it came back with nothing in his hands and said he is not going to come a third time. In the third week of the second month a woman of twenty-four worked out that a person with something behind her is not available and told nobody. In the last chapter the arrangement is still standing.**

**And the outline of record's own sentence about the box is false, and the page said so in a mouth two batches ago.** `outline/volume-09.md:115` and the concrete-resolution field both say that a box of about four hundred blanks is *the only supply* of a thing that is bought about four hundred a year. **Chapter 0410 has Marn Ottery say, in her own mouth at that counter, that the box is not the supply, and Chapter 0422 has the man who comes in on the second of the two days say he has wanted to know where the case is filled for about nine years, and neither of those is contradicted anywhere in this volume.** The supply is the case at the near end. The box is a thing of about four hundred unfilled blanks under a counter for eleven years with dust on the lid. **This batch therefore did not write the outline's sentence, and the box moves on the page as what the page says it is — a thing nobody can account for — and the cost of moving it is entered in a person and not in a figure, exactly as the outline asks, and the cost is that the carrier is now a man a courier saw on a road.** The wrong clause is named here and is deleted nowhere, and a close of this volume must not reinstate it.
